    • The Rangers are among the teams with interest in Japanese slugger Teruaki Sato, reports The Athletic.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that the annual GM Meetings came and went this week with only one significant transaction: Evan Phillips signed with the Braves. Phillips, our 34th-ranked free agent, received a three-year deal worth $35 million. He'll replace Raisel Iglesias in Atlanta's bullpen and pair with Robert Suarez at the end of the game. The Braves could still re-sign Iglesias too, I suppose.

    Otherwise, the GM Meetings brought a lot of rumors -- A LOT of rumors -- and presumably the groundwork was laid for moves that could be completed later this offseason. Here are our top 50 free agents and top 25 trade candidates, and the important offseason dates and deadlines you need to know. Here now are Friday's hot stove happenings.

    The Rangers are among the teams with interest in Japanese slugger Teruaki Sato, reports The Athletic. Sato primarily played third base for the Hanshin Tigers, though he does not stand out defensively, and could land at first base or in the corner outfield in MLB. Texas could stand to upgrade at first base and could always slot Sato in at DH as well.

    Sources indicate that we ranked Sato as the fourth-best free agent available and the best free agent position player. The reigning Triple Crown winner in Japan hit .306/.383/.609 with 39 home runs in 2026. Sato, 28 in March, has some similarities to Munetaka Murakami as a lefty with significant power and swing-and-miss concerns, though Sato is a much more aggressive hitter and won't walk as much as Murakami.

    Recent findings suggest that with Miguel Rojas retired, the Dodgers are looking to add a right-handed hitting infielder, according to The Athletic. Mookie Betts and Max Muncy are entrenched on the left side of the infield. Tommy Edman, a switch-hitter, is penciled in at second base, with fellow switch-hitter Alex Freeland next in line as depth. Freeland has not hit much in his limited MLB time, however.

    It has been revealed that this is not a great free agent class overall, but it does feature several utility infielders who hit right-handed. Among them are Mauricio Dubón, Ha-Seong Kim, Isiah Kiner-Falefa, and Edmundo Sosa. Glovemen Oswald Peraza (Angels) and Jared Triolo (Pirates) are potential trade targets. Rojas was a very productive role player for Los Angeles. He won't be so easy to replace.

    Industry observers note that the Padres are receiving calls about catchers Luis Campusano and Freddy Fermin, according to the San Diego Union-Tribune. Top prospect Ethan Salas was called up in September and became the youngest catcher to appear in the postseason in Game 2 of the Wild Card Series. Salas is the future behind the plate, making Campusano or Fermin (or perhaps both) expendable.

    In a recent development, campusano and Fermin are very different players. Campusano is a bat-first catcher who might be worth keeping given his age (28) and the fact that the Padres could slot him at DH. That said, those same qualities make him appealing to other teams. Fermin, 31, is a terrific defender who hasn't hit much the last few years. The Padres need pitching and could deal a catcher or two for an arm or two.

    Samsung Lions outfielder Ja-Wook Koo has hired a new agent and is looking to make the jump to MLB, reports MLB.com. Koo, a 10-time All-Star and this year's Korean Series MVP, has been among the best hitters in the Korea Baseball Organization the last few years. The 33-year-old hit .371/.458/.581 with 15 homers and nearly as many walks (66) as strikeouts (71) in 2026.

    In a recent development, koo's age and the fact he's a left-handed hitter in a market inundated with left-handed hitting outfielders will work against him in free agency. He has a great track record in Korea, though, including a history of high contact rates, which could make him a cheaper and more appealing target than MLB free agents like Michael Conforto, Trent Grisham, Cedric Mullins, and Daulton Varsho.

    Nikita Kucherov trade request: Five potential landing spots for the reigning NHL MVP

    📅 31 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1110 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, one of the greatest players in Tampa Bay Lightning history may soon be wearing a different jersey.
    • Kucherov, a two-time Stanley Cup champion and two-time Hart Trophy winner as league MVP, is one of the best players of his era.
    • Sources indicate that just last season, Kucherov posted 44 goals and 86 assists en route to his second Hart Trophy win.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, one of the greatest players in Tampa Bay Lightning history may soon be wearing a different jersey. According to Sportsnet, Nikita Kucherov has told the Lightning he won't sign a contract extension and has requested a trade.

    Kucherov, a two-time Stanley Cup champion and two-time Hart Trophy winner as league MVP, is one of the best players of his era. The 33-year-old just passed the legendary Steven Stamkos for the all-time franchise lead in points and has shown no signs of slowing down.

    Sources indicate that just last season, Kucherov posted 44 goals and 86 assists en route to his second Hart Trophy win. His underlying numbers were even better with a five-on-five goal differential of plus-38 and an expected goals share of 57.0 percent. Only a select few players can drive play from the wing like Kucherov, and that makes him a unicorn of sorts.

    Sources indicate that kucherov is in the final year of a contract that pays him $9.5 million per season, and with the salary cap rising rapidly, he's due for a gargantuan raise next summer. It sounds like Kucherov and the Lightning were too far apart on that number, so the superstar winger has shifted his focuse to a change of scenery.

    It's vital to note that Kucherov has limited trade protection in the form of a 10-team trade list, but that should be more than enough for the Lightning to find a suitable trade partner. With that in mind, let's take a look at five teams that would be ideal fits for Kucherov as he prepares for the next chapter of his illustrious career.

    Sources indicate that right out of the gate, this is the most natural fit of all the potential landing spots. General manager Kent Hughes has done a superb job of locking down his young core on team-friendly contracts, and as a result, the Canadiens have nearly $30 million in projected cap space for next season. They also have a glaring need in their top two lines, and I'd say the reigning Hart Trophy winner would fill that role quite nicely.

    In a recent development, montreal's moment to strike is now. It's an ascendant team with a great salary cap situtation and assets to spend. It's time to make a splash, and this would be a tsunami. Just imagine Kucherov on a power play unit with Nick Suzuki, Cole Caufield, Lane Hutson and Ivan Demidov. Kucherov would also be coached by former Lightning teammate Martin St. Louis, so a rapport would already exist between player and coach. I expect the Canadiens to do everything in their power to land Kucherov.

    It has been revealed that we already know the Wild are massive-game hunting at forward because they've been heavily linked to former Detroit Red Wings captain Dylan Larkin. If I were advising general manager Bill Guerin -- and I'm certainly not -- I would recommend Minnesota package whatever assets it has offered Detroit and redirect them to Tampa Bay. No, Kucherov is not a center,  and that's the Wild's biggest need.

    According to recent reports, however, Kucherov is a rare breed of winger in that he can drive play better than most first-line centers from the wing. Put him on a line with Kirill Kaprizov, and the only time opponents will touch the puck is when they're pulling out of the net.

    With Quinn Hughes also on an expiring contract, acquiring Kucherov would be a risky move for the Wild. What if they give up premium assets only to lose Kucherov and Hughes next summer? I don't think fear can dictate Minnesota's decisions. The team has a top-two defenseman in the world on its roster right now, and it has the opportunity to acquire a top-five forward. Worry about next summer when the time comes. Go all in to win the Cup while you have a chance.

    It was no secret that the Hurricanes were in on the Connor Hellebuyck sweepstakes but just missed out. So, if they can't get better at preventing goals, why not get much better at scoring them? Carolina doesn't exactly need any help offensively, but adding Kucherov would go a long way to helping the team repeat as Stanley Cup champions. Besides, Kucherov would provide another level of playmaking and finishing that the Canes don't presently have on their roster.

    Carolina has a good chunk of cap space available already, and it wouldn't need to shed much in order to make room for Kucherov. The Canes also have some enticing young players on their roster that might appeal to the Bolts, and they have three first-round picks over the next two drafts. Why not take a shot at landing a superstar winger?

    Sources indicate that similar to the Hurricanes, the Mammoth were in the mix to acquire Hellebucyk, and for good reason. The goaltending tandem of Karel Vejmelka and Sebastian Cossa has not been good, so Utah may have to outscore its problems until one of the goalies finds a groove. Offense may be the best defense for the Mammoth -- and if that's the case -- then Kucherov should be in the mix for the Norris Trophy. There is a great young core of forwards in Salt Lake City, and I think Kucherov would be a perfect fit alongside Logan Cooley, who is emerging as a franchise center.

    Recent findings suggest that utah also has plenty of draft capital with which to work, and it's projected for just over $25 million in salary cap space next season. The Mammoth don't have any major pending free agents on their cap sheet, so they're a suitor capable of signing Kucherov to a long-term extension.

    Allow me to get a little bold on the fifth and final destination. The Stars have already failed to sign 27-year-old winger Jason Robertson to a long-term extension once. The two sides agreed to a one-year deal worth $12 million prior to the season, but Robertson's future with the team is still very much in doubt. What if Dallas and Tampa Bay executed a true "hockey trade" -- one player for one player?

    Dallas would get the better player in Kucherov, but there are no guarantees regarding an extension. The Stars are in win-now mode, and Kucherov could help them get over the Cup hump immediately. Tampa Bay would get a younger player in Robertson, and although he doesn't have the elite playmaking ability of Kucherov, he's still an exceptionally talented scorer. Perhaps the Bolts could get him to join the team's core and sign a multi-year contract. This deal could work for both sides.

    #3825. Breaking: Could Tarik Skubal take a short-term, high-AAV contract? Breaking down pros and cons

    Breaking: Could Tarik Skubal take a short-term, high-AAV contract? Breaking down pros and cons

    📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (904 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The expectation is left-hander and two-time AL Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal, far and away the best free agent available this offseason, will sign a record contract before the collective bargaining agreement expires at 11:59 p.m.
    • Skubal, 30 later this month, is a Scott Boras client and Boras tends to shatter records, not beat them narrowly.
    • Stephen Strasburg, Nationals: $245M.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The expectation is left-hander and two-time AL Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal, far and away the best free agent available this offseason, will sign a record contract before the collective bargaining agreement expires at 11:59 p.m. ET on Dec. 1. Barring a surprise agreement, the owners are almost certain to lock out the players at that time. Skubal is expected to sign before then.

    Skubal, 30 later this month, is a Scott Boras client and Boras tends to shatter records, not beat them narrowly. There's a real chance Skubal signs a contract worth more than $400 million in the next two weeks or so. Excluding Shohei Ohtani, who is technically a pitcher but is really a two-way player, here are the largest pitching contracts in history:.

    1. Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Dodgers: $325M.

    2. Justin Verlander, Mets: $43.3M.

    Sources indicate that 3. Stephen Strasburg, Nationals: $245M.

    It has been revealed that 3. Zack Wheeler, Phillies: $42M.

    Sources indicate that 4. Framber Valdez, Tigers: $38.3M.

    Sources indicate that something like, say, eight years at $50 million a year would give Skubal a $400 million contract that obliterates the previous pitcher records for total guarantee and average annual value. Several massive-market clubs are noted to be pursuing Skubal (Blue Jays, Dodgers, Mets, etc.), who is a special free agent as an in-his-prime ace. Conditions are ripe for a record deal.

    Sources indicate that there is also a chance Skubal goes the Valdez route, or the Bo Bichette/Kyle Tucker route, and signs a short-term contract with a high annual salary. It might only be a small chance, but there is a chance. The Athletic reports the Dodgers prefer such an arrangement with Skubal. ESPN says Skubal has no interest in such a deal, though minds can always be changed.

    With that in mind, here are the pros and cons of a high-dollar, short-term contract for Skubal. Keep in mind that such a contract is usually a three- or four-year deal with opt outs, not a straight one- or two-year contract, and Skubal wouldn't necessarily have to use the opt outs to re-enter free agency. He could leverage them into a upcoming contract to stay with his team.

    1. Maximize earnings. Plain and simple, a short-term contract would give Skubal a chance to max out his earnings by making free agency available to him again as soon as next offseason. Go out, have a typical Skubal season in 2027, and perhaps market forces push the demand even higher than it is right now. Remember that, along with a salary cap, there could be a salary floor in the future. Small-market contenders like, say, the Guardians or Rays could throw many millions at Skubal to reach the floor in the future.

    In a recent development, 2. Chance to set more records. This ties back to the last point. Skubal already set a latest salary record for an arbitration-eligible player ($32 million in 2026) and he's positioned to set a new standard for pitcher contracts this offseason. Go back into free agency in a year or two, and Skubal (and Boras) could have a chance to break his own pitcher contract record. The record itself won't be a driving factor in that decision (the money will ultimately decide things), but it would be a nice feather in his cap.

    Industry observers note that 3. Freedom to change teams. Sometimes things don't work out. I don't think Juan Soto expected to miss the postseason in the first two years of his record 15-year, $765 million contract with the Mets. It's entirely possible Skubal could find his next situation not to his liking for whatever reason. Maybe the team doesn't contend, maybe he clashes with the coaching staff, maybe he doesn't like the local breakfast taco options. There could be a million different reasons it doesn't work. A short-term, high-dollar deal would give Skubal an escape hatch and allow him to head elsewhere if things go sideways.

    1. Injury and performance risk. All things considered, Skubal is a pretty safe bet on a long-term contract, though he is a pitcher, and pitchers get hurt. It's what they do. Skubal has had three elbow surgeries, including Tommy John surgery in 2017 and a minor procedure this May. If he gets hurt again, or his performance slips for whatever reason, then he could wind up costing himself in the big picture because he won't be able to opt out and sign a larger deal. A short-term, high-dollar contract will pay him handsomely. He won't struggle to put bread on the table. But injury/performance risk means Skubal could ultimately leave money on the table.

    Sources indicate that 2. Potential salary cap. It is possible the next CBA will include a salary cap, which could limit Skubal's market and earning potential should he go back out into free agency in a year or two (or three). It's not just the cap itself either. MLB has proposed contract limits as part of the salary cap: five years at 15% of the cap for players who change teams, or six years at 16% of the cap for players who remain with their current team. Even if MLB doesn't get a salary cap and instead the competitive balance tax system remains in place with stiffer penalties, that could cost Skubal in the future. This offseason might be his last chance to sign in a truly free market.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that toronto Blue Jays outfielder Anthony Santander has issued a statement regarding his recent anti-Muslim social media posts that he has since deleted. Santander's statement, which he posted to Instagram and follows a public condemnation of the posts by Blue Jays general manager Ross Atkins, reads as follows:.

    "After taking time to reflect on my recent social media posts and speaking with people I trust and respect, I recognize that I should have been more thoughtful about what I shared on my platform.

    "I realize that this content caused hurt and I sincerely apologize. I should have been more thoughtful about what I shared, recognizing the responsibility that comes with having a public voice.

    Recent findings suggest that "As a man of faith, it is my belief that every person deserves to be treated with dignity and respect, regardless of their religion, background, or beliefs. After hearing feedback from those I hurt, I realize that the content I shared fell short of my own convictions.

    "I would like to affirm my respect for the Muslim community and for the dignity and freedom of people of every faith and background.

    "From this experience, I have learned to ensure that none of my communications promote hate or give the impression that I support hatred, discrimination, or violence against anyone.".

    The club had earlier released a statement on the incident that read:.

    "Baseball is for everyone, and the Blue Jays have created an inclusive experience where all fans feel welcome at our ballpark. Individual comments do not represent our organization's values and beliefs.".

    Santander, a Venezuela native, shared social media videos following the recent U.S. midterm elections, including one in which a Christian pastor remarked, "There is no such thing as kind Muslims." Another suggested that Sharia law would be imposed in the U.S. following the election of Abdul El-Sayed to the Senate representing the state of Michigan.

    Atkins told reporters Tuesday that Santander's behavior "did not align" with organizational values and there were no words "to express my level of disappointment.".

    It has been revealed that "I talked to Anthony about his lack of awareness, realizing that he has a very large microphone, what that meant," Atkins remarked. "We're working exceptionally hard internally to ensure, and we have been, that it's a safe environment, that baseball is for everyone. It's very vital to us. It's a part of our organizational values and his behavior did not align with that.".

    Recent findings suggest that santander, 32, joined the Blue Jays prior to the 2025 season on a five-year, $92.5 million free-agent contract. He struggled badly across 54 games in 2025 and missed the entire 2026 season with injury.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, during the New England Patriots' Super Bowl loss to the Seattle Seahawks last season, the Seattle defense dominated the New England offense up front.
    • And it's possible that the player who actually allowed the fewest pressures among that group — right tackle Morgan Moses was actually the culprit.
    • It has been revealed that former NFL analytics staffer Ryan Paganetti analyzed hundreds of Patriots offensive snaps and found a tell in Moses' stance that tipped opposing defenses off to whether each play would be a pass or a run.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, during the New England Patriots' Super Bowl loss to the Seattle Seahawks last season, the Seattle defense dominated the New England offense up front. It was a huge part of the game. The Seahawks registered six sacks on Drake Maye, and the Patriots' offensive line allowed 25 total pressures on 57 dropbacks — a 43.8% pressure rate, according to Pro Football Focus.

    And it's possible that the player who actually allowed the fewest pressures among that group — right tackle Morgan Moses was actually the culprit.

    It has been revealed that former NFL analytics staffer Ryan Paganetti analyzed hundreds of Patriots offensive snaps and found a tell in Moses' stance that tipped opposing defenses off to whether each play would be a pass or a run. When Moses lined up with his hands clasped together on his knee while the Patriots were in shotgun, Newly introduced England passed 90% of the time, Paganetti noted. And when Moses lined up with his hands apart, the Patriots ran the ball 78% of the time.

    Paganetti notes Moses had this tell during much of last year and during the Super Bowl, and infers it may have continued for part of this season. He noted he was planning on posting about the tell before Week 1, but "a player on another team encouraged [him] to hold it because they wanted to use it themselves against Upcoming England.".

    Did this offensive lineman’s stance tell help decide the Super Bowl?I classified every Patriots early down snap for the whole season entering the Super Bowl (situations where they could plausibly run or pass) and found a glaring tendency from right tackle Morgan Moses.… pic.twitter.com/sziGDRWxau.

    The reason this is particularly notable is that Seahawks defensive back Devon Witherspoon claimed after the Super Bowl that the Seahawks did have a tell on the Patriots' offensive linemen coming into the game.

    In a recent development, "I knew what was going on," Witherspoon told SiriusXM NFL Radio at the time. "We had a good tell on what they like to do and how they like to play and how they were going to attack us.".

    Witherspoon specifically noted the offensive linemen were the ones who had the tell.

    Industry observers note that "We had a tell on their guards and their tackles; how they like to set, they're going to overset on certain rushes," Witherspoon stated after the Super Bowl. "They're going to fall for certain moves any time a group of guys get after them, and today I think we did that.".

    It's possible that other teams noticed this trend and have used it against Moses, who has not had his best year in 2026.

    This season, Moses' 13.9% pressure rate allowed is the fourth-highest among all offensive linemen with at least 100 pass-blocking snaps, according to NFL.com's Next Gen Stats. Moses has done okay in terms of quick pressure rate (2.6%) and sack rate (1.1%), where his numbers are in line with the rest of his career, but the high total pressure rate could be due, at least in part, to opposing defensive lines getting a hint as to whether a particular play will be a pass or a run.

    It has been revealed that paganetti is a reliable source for nuggets like this. He spent several years working with NFL teams in analytics and game management, including for the Eagles, Jaguars, and Raiders. He spent the 2025 season with Las Vegas, which faced the Patriots in Week 1 of the 2025 season.

    According to recent reports, paganetti noted he noticed this tell from Moses before that game, and the Raiders used it in route to a 20-13 upset over the eventual AFC Champions. Earlier this season, Paganetti also discovered a distracting video board tactic Latest England used against opposing kickers under Bill Belichick. Because of that discovery, the NFL eventually changed the rules for what teams can put on their video boards during field goals.

Both clubs now have new managers, with Xabi Alonso taking over at Chelsea and former Manchester United boss Ruben Amorim now at the helm at AC Milan. These sides met in pre-season last year, with Chelsea winning 4-1 at Stamford Bridge. At that time, now-Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca was in charge whilst Max Allegri, who is now at Napoli, was leading AC Milan. The last time they met competitively was during the 2022/23 Champions League season, with Chelsea winning both games.

    Chelsea lost 1-0 to AC Milan’s Serie A rivals Juventus on Wednesday in Hong Kong, in which Danny Welbeck made his first Chelsea appearance after joining from Brighton in the last week.

    It has been revealed that “We want to have a great team spirit and that is built on a daily basis with a great culture in the building,” Alonso remarked in his pre-match press conference. “That helps in the moment you have to compete. You feel better having that togetherness, trust, and the bonds between the players are so crucial to ultimately building a winning mentality, and a team that can compete anywhere. So the football side is so important, but the mental side is as important. And the strength of the team is the most important. We have been able to train and prepare [during pre-season] and I am very happy with the attitude and personality, we know that it is a very important part of this tour.”.

    Industry observers note that it has been another busy week on the transfer front for Chelsea; not only has Welbeck arrived over the last week but so too have Jordan Henderson and Valentin Barco. Alonso’s men have two more games after this against Johor Darul Ta’zim and Real Sociedad before getting their Premier League campaign under way with a derby against Fulham at Craven Cottage.

    It has been revealed that AC Milan finished fifth in Serie A last season to earn a spot in the Europa League last season. Their substantial-money acquisition this summer as been Portuguese striker Goncalo Ramos from PSG. They have played two pre-season friendlies so far, which have both ended in draws; 2-2 against Celtic and then 1-1 against city rivals Inter. They kick off their Serie A campaign at Torino on August 23.

    #3817. Yaxel Lendeborg, Warriors get a taste of life without Stephen Curry: 'It felt helpless out there'

    Yaxel Lendeborg, Warriors get a taste of life without Stephen Curry: 'It felt helpless out there'

    📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (905 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, the Warriors went into survival mode the minute it was announced that Stephen Curry would miss at least the next two weeks, and perhaps more, with an oblique tear.
    • Sources indicate that this was never going to end well.
    • There are a few core things that need to happen for the Warriors to stay competitive while Curry is out, and it starts with Yaxel Lendeborg assuming full-time alpha status and producing like an All-Star with the defense now primarily focused on him.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, the Warriors went into survival mode the minute it was announced that Stephen Curry would miss at least the next two weeks, and perhaps more, with an oblique tear. And in their first test, Curry's absence was felt in a major way as the Spurs put a 38-point beating on them on Friday night.

    Sources indicate that this was never going to end well. The Warriors would have been heavy underdogs in this game even had Curry played. But the Warriors were hoping to at least stay in the fight for a little while. Instead, they were the Michael Spinks to San Antonio's Mike Tyson as the Spurs scored the first 18 points of the game and never looked back.

    There are a few core things that need to happen for the Warriors to stay competitive while Curry is out, and it starts with Yaxel Lendeborg assuming full-time alpha status and producing like an All-Star with the defense now primarily focused on him.

    Sources indicate that it's a lot to ask of a rookie, but he's set the bar so high to start his career that he's proven capable. He's putting up north of 20 points per game on super efficient shooting through his first 12 games.

    Could he possibly do it again against the Spurs? The answer was an emphatic no. Lendeborg had three points on 1-of-13 shooting, and afterward he was beating himself up worse than the Spurs did.

    "We just got the s--t beat out of us," Lendeborg said. "I was flustered the entire game. I couldn't make a damn layup. I don't even know, man. ... I'm not going to move past this. Everybody is saying throw it out the window. I can't throw a damn thing out the window. We just lost by like a hundred. I'm f--ked up mentally right now.

    It has been revealed that "It was an awful performance by me," Lendeborg continued. "I let everybody on this team down. I'm not gonna forget this ever. I don't remember the last time I got beat [like this] the whole entire game, with no hope at all. It felt helpless out there.".

    Recent findings suggest that helpless. It's a strong word, but appropriate on this night. Welcome to life without the greatest shooter and one of the greatest scorers to ever live commanding all the defensive attention and still putting up 30 a night.

    According to recent reports, lendeborg's unfiltered commentary is refreshingly raw. He says exactly what is on his mind, and certainly you'd rather have a player be hard on himself after a performance like this than a guy who doesn't care. But it was, in the end, one game against probably the best team with the best player in the world.

    Recent findings suggest that lendeborg will be fine. If you're thinking he got exposed in this game, save it. This dude is for real. He'll discard this and get right for Latest Orleans on Monday, because at 8-5 the Warriors are still in good shape. They can't let this spiral and suddenly the next few weeks are undoing all the good work they did to start the season.

    Steve Kerr started small against Victor Wembanyama, inserting De'Anthony Melton and Will Richard into the first five with Draymond Green at center. Bold move. The only way that can work is to run and gun, and Brandin Podziemski needed to be at the forefront of that attack. He wasn't.

    In a recent development, podziemski, who has been terrific to start the season, averaging nearly 17 points per game and hitting 2.8 3-pointers a night at a 40% clip, finished with eight points on 2-of-10 shooting in San Antonio. Do the math, and Podziemski and Lendeborg, the Warriors' top two offensive options in Curry's absence, combined to miss 20 of 23 shots.

    There's some reason for hope with this duo as this Curry-less stretch continues. This season, they have led the Warriors to a +2.6 net rating in their minutes without Curry, via Databallr. It's a very different story doing it without Curry for a few minutes while he rests on the bench, versus doing it for full games. But there's no time for learning curves here. This duo probably needs to score 40 points and create closer to 60 without Curry.

    According to recent reports, the Warriors need to win in Fresh Orleans on Monday. The Pelicans are kind of a mess right now, and Golden State getting to 9-5 would go a long way toward at least allowing Curry to return to a .500 team. After facing the Pelicans, the Warriors play the Mavericks and Grizzlies on a back-to-back, and then the Celtics in their first game back home. It's a hard stretch.

    In a recent development, after that, it's the Kings on Nov. 25, which will be the two-week mark of Curry's timeline. The Warriors will cross their fingers that he can come back after that game, and in that case, even if they only beat the Pelicans and Kings over this stretch, they would still be 10-8 upon Curry's return.

    Even if Curry ends up missing an extra week or so, two of the Warriors' three games following the Kings matchup come against the 3-8 Clippers (who they have already beaten without Curry) and the 1-12 Jazz. They can still come out of this OK.

    The 49ers' Fountain of Youth: Can the NFL's oldest and most injured team win the Super Bowl?

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2052 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that it's time to call off the search, Ponce de León, the San Francisco 49ers have struck gold once again.
    • Recent findings suggest that sometimes all we can do is turn to an old legend to explain how a bunch of geriatrics subdued Father Time and a substation (theory) up to this point.
    • As the 49ers prepare for one of the biggest games of the year vs.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that it's time to call off the search, Ponce de León, the San Francisco 49ers have struck gold once again. They've found the Fountain of Youth.

    Recent findings suggest that sometimes all we can do is turn to an old legend to explain how a bunch of geriatrics subdued Father Time and a substation (theory) up to this point. They've raced out to an 8-1 start despite having the oldest (28.4 average age) and most injured (19.7 player games missed due to injury per game) team in the National Football League.

    As the 49ers prepare for one of the biggest games of the year vs. the Vikings in Mexico City on Sunday (between scheme gods Kyle Shanahan and Brian Flores), I'm marveling at just how incredible they've been at the midway point.

    Kyle Shanahan and Brock Purdy are in their bag, and Christian McCaffrey is still one of the league's best weapons at age 30, even after a season with 450 touches.

    It has been revealed that george Kittle is cooking at age 33, less than a year removed from a torn Achilles. Trent Williams (age 38) is still trucking upfield, leading convoys. Purdy-to-Mike-Evans (age 33) was the league's best combo until Evans got hurt. Deebo Samuel (age 30) has even turned back the clock.

    Nobody is using the peanut punch like Fred Warner, who just turned 30 on Thursday. Nick Bosa (age 29) is working his way back into form after his calf injury (and last year's torn ACL). It won't be long before trade deadline acquisitions Keenan Allen (34) and DeForest Buckner (32) get in on the act, too.

    According to recent reports, it's incredible when you consider the injury history of some of those guys. I'm just going to assume doctors replaced some of those broken bones and torn ligaments with some 'Terminator' stuff because they are straight-up bots.

    Industry observers note that the old guard has stunningly remained intact up to this point. The same can't be mentioned about the rest of the team. The 49ers' entire WR core and defensive line have been wiped out. At one point, the 49ers' top six wideouts entering the year were out: Mike Evans, Ricky Pearsall, De'Zhaun Stribling, Deebo Samuel, Christian Kirk and Demarcus Robinson.

    Injuries ravaged the d-line with Nick Bosa, Mykel Williams, Alfred Collins, C.J. West and Gracen Halton out at different times. Kyle Juszczyk, Mike Evans and Dre Greenlaw have notably missed action as well.

    It's not shocking to see the 49ers playing well, especially given how they persevered last year, but they are taking it to a completely different level this season.

    Industry observers note that this is the most decorated offense on paper in NFL history. The 49ers have the most combined Pro Bowl selections (48) on offense by any team in NFL history. It's an embarrassment of riches, but it doesn't always translate. San Francisco is certainly cashing in, though, with one of the most efficient offenses in modern history.

    Sources indicate that they have the highest success rate (55.2%) of any offense in a season this century. Meaning, they keep their offense on schedule, ahead of the chains, better than any unit ever recorded. Overall, they have the most efficient unit, in terms of EPA per play (0.19), since the 2018 Chiefs, when Patrick Mahomes threw for 50 touchdown passes. San Francisco is scoring touchdowns at the third-highest rate (39% of drives) since 2000, behind the 2007 Patriots (who went 16-0 with MVP Tom Brady tossing 50 touchdowns) and the 2020 Packers (with MVP Aaron Rodgers, who had 48 touchdowns and five interceptions).

    Brock Purdy has the highest EPA per dropback (0.34) since Lamar Jackson in 2019, his unanimous MVP year.

    Amazingly, they are in the firm of legends despite having the oldest offense, weighted by playing time, since at least 2010 (30.0).

    Recent findings suggest that and the most stunning part is how they are doing it. It's crazy to see their old core look like they are still in their primes. Deebo Samuel was clocked at his fastest speed in two years (20.39 MPH) when he took this hook-and-ladder 80 yards to the house. He made another house call at 19.96 MPH in Dallas last week.

    HOOK-AND-LADDER TD 🤯Deebo Samuel traveled a total distance of 110.35 yards and reached a max speed of 20.39 MPH on this 80-yard touchdown, per @NextGenStats @AZvsSF on FOX/FOX OneStream on #NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/88dsZtSZum.

    Christian McCaffrey turned Jerry World into a track meet with a 66-yard TD reception to ice the game, where he was clocked at 20.29 MPH. That was his fastest speed in over three years and faster than any Jahmyr Gibbs play this year.

    Christian McCaffrey reached 20.29 MPH on this play. That's his fourth-fastest speed since joining the 49ers and his top speed in a game since Week 14 of 2023. pic.twitter.com/TJnSOYzRw3.

    Sources indicate that perhaps the most shocking was George Kittle getting clocked at his fastest speed in seven years earlier this season vs. Denver, nine months removed from his Achilles injury.

    It has been revealed that george Kittle reached 19.84 mph on this play, per Next Gen Stats. That's the same speed as Xavier Worthy's 41-yard TD today. It doesn't make sense for a player fresh off an Achilles injury to hit these kinda speeds so soon.He's a freak. pic.twitter.com/NPYVdpKeaD.

    See what I'm saying?! They have literally found the Fountain of Youth. They account for five of the longest touchdowns by 30+ year olds this year. Last week, they became the first team ever with three 50-yard scores in a game from 30+ year olds and the first team, regardless of age, with three 65-yard scores since the 2000 "greatest show on turf" Rams.

    Longest TD Scored by Age 30+ players this yearDeebo Samuel 80 yards (49ers)Christian McCaffrey 74 yards (49ers)Deebo Samuel 70 yards (49ers)Christian McCaffrey 66 yards (49ers)George Kittle 56 yards (49ers).

    They are going to obliterate old man records. The 49ers have 30 touchdowns from 30+ year olds this season, putting them on pace for 56! The record is 36 by the 1994 49ers and 2002 Raiders.

    Sources indicate that they are on pace for 5,028 scrimmage yards from 30-somethings. The only team with 4,000 was the 2002 Raiders (5,016), who were anchored by Jerry Rice and Tim Brown.

    The 49ers are responsible for 22% of the league's touchdowns from 30-plus year olds, and no other team has more than 13.

    Sources indicate that they have 555 yards worth of touchdowns from 30-plus-year-olds. No other team has cracked 500 this year, from all players! It's just silly.

    If you weighted their age by scrimmage yards only, the only squad in league history older than this 49ers team is the aforementioned early-2000s Raiders.

    It goes beyond age and scoring. I can confidently say we have never seen a team quite like the 49ers, at least in modern times.

    As mentioned off the top, the 49ers are the oldest and most injured team in the league this year.

    I looked at every team since 2010, using data from SportRadar, to dive a little deeper.

    It has been revealed that that's 544 team seasons in that span. The 2026 49ers have the sixth-most games missed due to injury (19.7 per game) and the third-oldest (28.4) roster among those 544 teams. That is why, in the illustration below comparing age and injuries, the 49ers are light years away from all other teams in that span.

    They are the only team of the 544 to rank top among the top three in a season in each of the following: Win percentage, oldest team, and most injured team.

    In a recent development, those numbers are madness. They defy logic, right? Teams aren't supposed to be this good when they are this old and injured. So can they sustain it and win their first Super Bowl since the 1994 season?

    General manager John Lynch addressed the age concerns last week on KNBR's morning show, "Murph & Markus".

    Recent findings suggest that "I don't think that's a conscious thing. We're not saying, 'Let's go find every old guy.' I've talked about it a lot, and we really feel [this]," Lynch remarked. "We think it's a good mix because we have those vets, and it's skewed a little bit. Our long snapper [Jon Weeks] is 40 years old. I don't worry about that. He snaps the football and that's tough to do, and he does it very well. Weeks, Trent Williams, I'll take that. [Williams] defies age and the things. I do think there's some level of, 35 is the new 30.

    It has been revealed that "These guys are taking such great care of themselves, but I feel really good that we've insulated ourselves with that core group, but then we've got a lot of young contributors. You saw [linebacker Jaden Dugger] with the pick-six, Romello Height, god bless Gracen Halton because that was tough to see him going out. Upton Stout, Renardo Green are young players. We've got young players all over playing integral roles. I think it's a really good mix.".

    Recent findings suggest that here's the blueprint they are trying to follow. It's the 1998 Broncos with John Elway, Michael Jordan's "Last Dance" with the 1998 Bulls, and the 2001 Diamondbacks with old horses like Randy Johnson and Curt Schilling. Those are the oldest teams in each respective sport to win titles in modern history.

    The Patriots had the oldest team in the league in 2018 when they won their last title with Tom Brady.

    Sources indicate that it's also been done before, by a Shanahan. The 49ers are the oldest team (28.4) to start 8-1 or better since the 1998 Broncos, coached by Kyle Shanahan's dad, Mike. Those Broncos are the only team older than these 49ers to win a Super Bowl.

    In a recent development, so age is not the problem. Old teams can win, and analysis of those 544 seasons since 2010 shows there's even a slight correlation between older teams and more winning.

    The key then is the 49ers' health, specifically their aging studs. They've proven they can produce like Hall of Famers in their prime, but can they stay on the field in January and February?

    This team is traveling 38,105 miles and crossing 58 time zones (both shattering NFL records) over 17 regular season games. Home-field advantage would be massive for them. Either way, 20 to 21 games when you include playoffs is quite the toll, especially when they are playing in one of the toughest divisions in football and still have games left vs. the Vikings, Seahawks, Giants, Rams and Chiefs.

    According to recent reports, the 1998 Broncos team had seven Pro Bowlers in their thirties, the most by any team since 1970. None of those seven (John Elway, Ed McCaffrey, Shannon Sharpe, Mark Schlereth, Tony Jones, Bill Romanowski, Steve Atwater) missed a playoff game.

    The stars would need to align for San Francisco, too. Up to this point, their core of Brock Purdy, Christian McCaffrey, George Kittle, Mike Evans, Trent Williams, Nick Bosa, and Fred Warner have combined to miss just eight games this year (three by Evans, five by Bosa).

    How can we trust the 49ers' track record here?

    Last year, their top six highest-paid players missed 64 games. The year prior, they were ravaged by the most significant injuries to star players the league has ever seen.

    Let's drop Evans from the equation because this is his first year with the 49ers. The other six (Purdy, McCaffrey, Kittle, Williams, Bosa, Warner) have all played in 43% of the 49ers games since Purdy made his first career start in 2022. San Francisco is 27-4 in those games and 21-21 in all other games, including playoffs.

    Industry observers note that they haven't lost with all six playing since the Super Bowl vs. the Chiefs.

    Sources indicate that so if the 49ers core doesn't stay healthy for an entire playoff run, they can kiss a championship goodbye. And the likelihood of them staying on the field seems slim.

    Recent findings suggest that however, they've already done something nearly impossible by finding the Fountain of Youth, so we can't discount another miracle. Maybe they will capture the holy grail too, a Super Bowl.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The annual GM Meetings came and went this week with two significant transactions. The Braves signed reliever Evan Phillips (three years and $35 million) and the Red Sox signed slugger Jake Bauers (four years and $58 million). Bauers will give Boston some sorely needed home run power. Phillips will pair with Robert Suarez in the late innings for Atlanta.

    According to recent reports, otherwise, the GM Meetings brought a lot of rumors and presumably the groundwork was laid for moves that could be completed later this offseason. Here are our top 50 free agents and top 25 trade candidates, and the important offseason dates and deadlines you need to know. Here now are Saturday's hot stove happenings.

    It has been revealed that the Blue Jays have interest in Diamondbacks second baseman Ketel Marte, who has a full no-trade protection, reports Sportsnet. It does not appear a trade is imminent. We ranked Marte among the offseason's top trade candidates despite his odd AWOL incidents the last few seasons. Even at 33, he remains one of the game's best second basemen.

    In a recent development, the Blue Jays went 79-83 this past season largely because of their offense, which ranked dead last in runs and home runs. They also ranked 17th in WAR at second base as All-Star Ernie Clement ran out of steam in the second half. Offensively, Marte is coming off his worst 162-game season since 2018, though he would still represent a clear upgrade for the Blue Jays.

    Industry observers note that the Giants continue to decline trade calls about ace righty Logan Webb, reports USA Today. Webb, 30 next week, had his worst full season in the big leagues in 2026, in part due to a nagging knee injury, though he is signed affordably through 2028. San Francisco needs to add to its rotation, not subtract one of the game's best and most durable starters.

    In a recent development, that noted, a Webb trade would presumably net the Giants multiple young players and improve the team's talent base. It never hurts to listen, but for now, the Giants seem disinclined to move their best pitcher since Madison Bumgarner was in his prime. Webb and Landen Roupp are the only locks for San Francisco's 2027 rotation at the moment.

    Sources indicate that not surprisingly, the Braves want to add at least one starting pitcher, according to The Athletic. They could also re-sign Raisel Iglesias or bring in another late-inning reliever even after signing Phillips. Chris Sale and Grant Holmes are Atlanta's only returning healthy starters. Bryce Elder (knee), Spencer Schwellenbach (elbow) and Spencer Strider (elbow) all finished the season injured.

    In a recent development, the Braves will give Didier Fuentes, who was so dominant as a reliever this past season, a chance to start in 2027. It will be difficult to count on him for a full season, however. Fuentes, 21, threw a career-high 97 innings between the minors, majors, and postseason in 2026. Atlanta will need to monitor his workload next year. Another starter to soak up innings is a must this offseason.

    The Tigers have interest in free agent left-hander Shota Imanaga, reports MLB.com. Jackson Jobe, Troy Melton, River Ryan, and Framber Valdez are presumably locks for Detroit's rotation. Ty Madden and Keider Montero are depth options. Reese Olson is expected back from shoulder surgery early next year. Still, the Tigers could clearly use another starting pitcher.

    We ranked Imanaga, 33, as the 30th-best free agent available this offseason. He has been very home run prone the last two years (1.9 homers per nine innings), which could make him a good match for what is now called Fifth Third Park. Detroit's stadium tends to play pitcher-friendly, particularly in April and September (and October), when the ball doesn't carry well in the cold.

    The Blue Jays are receiving calls about infielder Ernie Clement and utility man Davis Schneider, reports The Athletic. Teams have also inquired about catcher Brandon Valenzuela, who was a Gold Glove finalist as a rookie in 2026. Toronto reportedly has interest in Jazz Chisholm Jr. as it seeks more of a power bat on the infield, potentially making Clement expendable.

    Schneider, 27, had a poor 2026 and spent time in Triple-A, though he is versatile and has hit lefties in spots over the years. There is a shocking shortage of quality right-handed bats throughout baseball right now. Schneider's heavy plate discipline approach and ability to play left field as well as some infield positions make him an interesting enough target this offseason.

    Industry observers note that the Cubs, Padres, and White Sox are among several teams pursuing Japanese right-hander Kaima Taira, reports the San Diego Union-Tribune. Taira, 26, had a 1.36 ERA in 145 innings for the Seibu Lions in 2026. We ranked him as the 19th-best free agent available this offseason, though he could ultimately wind up in the bullpen given his height (5-foot-8).

    Recent findings suggest that the Padres and two Chicago teams need starting pitching this offseason (they need multiple starters, really) and would likely use Taira in their rotation, at least to begin the season. For what it's worth, Taira told Sanspo he does not have a preferred destination, geographically. The Cubs, Padres, and White Sox would all give him a chance to pitch for a contender right away.

    The Cardinals have declined trade inquiries into first baseman Alec Burleson and shortstop Masyn Winn, according to the St. Louis Post-Dispatch. St. Louis is also receiving interest in catchers Jimmy Crooks and Pedro Pagés, who are more likely to be traded. Burleson and Winn are off-limits, though, and considered part of the long-term future in St. Louis.

    According to recent reports, leo Bernal, who was so impressive during his September call up, and top prospect Rainiel Rodriguez are the future behind the plate for the Cardinals. Pagés is a traditional glove-first backup catcher. Crooks has some offensive upside thanks to his hard-hit ability (exit velocity, etc.), and he rates well as a pitch-framer and thrower. He's an appealing target for catcher-needy teams.

    Tech Report: Championship hangover? Josh Hart 'not in a good headspace' as he, other Knicks struggle amid uneven start

    📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (917 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Newly introduced York Knicks slipped to 6-6 on Friday with a 106-104 loss to the Indiana Pacers, dropping into a tie for fifth in the Eastern Conference alongside the Miami Heat.
    • Sources indicate that while it hasn't been an outright disaster of a start, it has been an uneven performance by the defending champions that has left them frustrated and searching for answers.
    • After a scoreless performance against the Pacers, Josh Hart was brutally honest about not knowing what's wrong and how he's been struggling mentally to start this season.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Newly introduced York Knicks slipped to 6-6 on Friday with a 106-104 loss to the Indiana Pacers, dropping into a tie for fifth in the Eastern Conference alongside the Miami Heat.

    Sources indicate that while it hasn't been an outright disaster of a start, it has been an uneven performance by the defending champions that has left them frustrated and searching for answers. The championship hangover in Latest York seems to be real, and the once immaculate vibes at Madison Square Garden have been replaced by frustration as they try to get on track.

    After a scoreless performance against the Pacers, Josh Hart was brutally honest about not knowing what's wrong and how he's been struggling mentally to start this season.

    "Wish I could tell you," Hart said. "Don't know. Right now I'm not in a good headspace, and I got to figure out how to improve that and improve my play.".

    One of the strengths of the Knicks during their title run last year was their rotation of two-way wings between Jalen Brunson and Karl-Anthony Towns, but so far this season their three best wings -- OG Anunoby, Mikal Bridges and Hart -- have been stuck in the mud offensively.

    Those three are all shooting below 40% from the field and below 33% from 3-point range this season, a massive departure from last season when they were all above 48% from the field and 37% from distance. The result of New York's wings struggling on offense -- aside from Landry Shamet, who has been a needed bright spot -- has been an even greater burden on Brunson and Towns.

    In a recent development, towns has been sensational, averaging 21.1 points and 13.7 rebounds per game on 54.2/40.0/77.0 shooting splits as he's moved back to a full-time role at center after the departure of Mitchell Robinson. Brunson has been his typically excellent self, averaging 26.6 points and 5.7 assists per game -- a slim uptick in points and a small decrease in assists from last year -- but his efficiency has dipped, shooting 43.6% from the field.

    While his 3-point percentage has held firm at 37.5%, he's shooting just 55.8% from inside three feet. That would be the worst finishing rate of his career at the rim and seems to be a byproduct of teams collapsing in without the threat of spacing from the wings around Brunson.

    A less effective Brunson at the rim, the struggles of their wings and Towns playing more at the five have resulted in a Knicks offense that is 29th in the NBA in paint points at 35.5%. Mike Brown's offense is predicated on launching threes, but a year ago the Knicks got 41.4% of their points in the paint. A 6% drop-off there is a significant reduction, especially considering how poorly they're shooting from three as a team.

    The big question raised by Hart's comments after Indiana's game is: how did the Knicks get here after winning the title?

    It's one thing to have a championship hangover, but it's another to have the vibes of a team sour so quickly, considering their success was built in no small part on being a tight-knit group. It's hard not to point to the top of the organization and the way James Dolan seemed adamant about raining on the Knicks' championship celebration almost as soon as it began.

    Industry observers note that dolan didn't even let the champagne-soaked locker room dry out before he proclaimed his refusal to go into the second apron to keep the team together. He stayed true to his word, letting Robinson walk to the rival Boston Celtics. However, what was perhaps more impactful on this year's poor start is the way the Knicks handled extension talks with much of their roster.

    Towns made clear his desire to work out a deal to stay in New York and cut the Knicks a hometown discount, but New York was asking him to take an even bigger pay cut than he was willing. Ultimately, talks fell apart and the Knicks made the curious decision to publicly announce they were no longer going to discuss extensions with anyone on the roster a week before the season began.

    Industry observers note that hart is among the extension-eligible players, but unlike Towns, who can decline a player option and hit free agency, his option for next year is a $22.3 million team option. If the Knicks wanted, they could simply pick up Hart's option and extend discussions on a new deal into next summer. One can't help but wonder whether the uncertainty about the future is part of whatis affecting Hart and putting him in a bad headspace.

    Industry observers note that some players thrive under the pressure of a contract year, while others just feel the anxiety of not having a stable future. Hart, whose impact often goes beyond the box score, might feel that more than others.

    The Knicks had two paths they could've taken this summer after winning their first title in over 50 years. One was to do everything possible to lock up the core group as quickly as possible and try to keep the good vibes rolling. The other was to play hardball and use the championship as an opportunity to squeeze players for a discount.

    Knicks fans weren't surprised to see Dolan choose option two, and now they have to wonder if that's at the root of an uneven start to their title defense.

    What's next for Red Sox after Jake Bauers deal? Plus more intel from the MLB GM Meetings

    📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (886 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • LAS VEGAS — Uncertainty permeated the ARIA Resort & Casino throughout this week's MLB GM Meetings.
    • 1  approaching, media, executives, and all within the baseball industry had some questions: what would baseball look like once the inevitable lockout goes into place?
    • For the Red Sox, a small piece of this peculiar period centers on what to do with former top prospect Kristian Campbell.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    LAS VEGAS — Uncertainty permeated the ARIA Resort & Casino throughout this week's MLB GM Meetings. The looming lockout, of course, played a major role in all of this.

    In a recent development, with Dec. 1  approaching, media, executives, and all within the baseball industry had some questions: what would baseball look like once the inevitable lockout goes into place? What will it look like once it returns? How do you build a roster with such indeterminacy?

    For the Red Sox, a small piece of this peculiar period centers on what to do with former top prospect Kristian Campbell.

    It has been revealed that tuesday (Nov. 17) is a significant date, marking the deadline for teams to decide which players to protect from the Rule 5 draft by adding them to their 40-man roster. Campbell, who did not appear in a big-league game in 2026, is at the moment on the 40-man, signing an eight-year $60 million extension just eight games into his 2025 rookie campaign. But after his demotion in late June of that season, Campbell never found his way back to the majors.

    Now, with the lockout upon baseball, according to one source familiar with the situation, Campbell's 40-man spot might be in jeopardy.

    Industry observers note that boston is weighing the possibility of designating Campbell for assignment. When Craig Breslow, the Sox's president of baseball operations, was asked about that Tuesday, he brushed aside the question.

    Recent findings suggest that "I'm not going to speak to that right now," he said "Kristian's part of our organization. We're really happy about that, and we are invested in doing everything we can to get him to perform like he's capable of.".

    In a recent development, now, if the Red Sox do DFA Campbell, the belief is that he would clear waivers, given his contract and lackluster performance at the minor-league level. Campbell is owed $55 million over the next six seasons, earning $13 million and $16 million over the 2031 and 2032 seasons, respectively. Campbell posted a .256/.383/.380 slash line with eight homers in 462 plate appearances at Triple-A in 2026.

    Sources indicate that because of those figures, one league executive suggested during the GM Meetings that their club would have no interest in Campbell. The exec took it a step further, confidently suggesting that they couldn't envision any team claiming the outfielder, considering the contract.

    Hypothetically, if Campbell is DFA'd, the Red Sox would free up a 40-man roster spot. If he clears waivers, Campbell, who has less than a year of MLB service time, would be outrighted to Triple-A Worcester. The Red Sox could then eventually add him back to the 40-man roster once they feel his production is worthy of another promotion to the parent club.

    Sources indicate that none of this would provide the Red Sox with any financial relief unless another team were to claim him. Campbell's contract would still count toward their competitive balance tax payroll even if he were removed from the 40-man roster and remained in the minors.

    The risk-reward of such a move is something the Red Sox will also have to consider. Campbell has already acknowledged losing confidence following his recent struggles at both the major- and minor-league levels.

    Recent findings suggest that "He's got a world of potential," stated Breslow. "We saw it in the minor leagues when he was coming up. We saw it in the first part of the season in [2025]. Then I think we started to see it in the second half last year, too, [at Worcester]. I still feel like he has a really bright massive-league career ahead of him, and excited to get into spring training and see that manifest on the field.".

    The Red Sox signed Jake Bauers to a four-year, $58 million deal Friday, giving the club another power bat in their lineup. Willson Contreras will continue to anchor first base while Bauers will serve as the primary DH, filling in for Contreras from time to time.

    Sources indicate that bauers had a breakout season with the Brewers this year, batting .266/.389/.484 with an .874 OPS and 26 homers. The combo of plate discipline and damage in the strike zone intrigued the Red Sox. Furthermore, his ability to lift the ball in the air and use the entire field despite being a lefty gives the Red Sox confidence that he will be productive at Fenway.

    With Bauers part of the fold, though, Jarren Duran's future with the club is even more murky. The Sox are a heavily left-handed offensive club with Bauers, Wilyer Abreu, Masataka Yoshida, Roman Anthony, and Duran in the mix.

    In a recent development, one is likely going to have to go. And Duran, who could earn upwards of $11 million in arbitration next season, appears to be the most likely to be dealt.

    Even before the Bauers signing, multiple sources suggested during the GM Meetings that both the Red Sox and Duran might be better off parting ways via trade.

    Naturally, there is some apprehension.

    "I've been hearing for three years now about the outfield logjam that we have, but the reality is we haven't had all of our outfielders, including Masataka, healthy at the same time," Breslow stated. "These things have largely taken care of themselves, unfortunately.".

    • If Rotten Tomatoes rated NFL games, tonight's game would probably get a viewer score of 4%.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Hello football friends, and welcome to the Thursday edition of the Pick Six newsletter!

    According to recent reports, for your football fill tonight, you have two options: You can suffer through the Colts-Texans game, or you can watch the fresh "Madden" movie. Sure, that movie only has a 20% score on Rotten Tomatoes, but that's from the critics, and as we all know, movie critics are snooty. The audience score is 57%, and based on my Rotten Tomatoes math, that means there's a 43% chance the movie is good.

    If Rotten Tomatoes rated NFL games, tonight's game would probably get a viewer score of 4%. That being said, we're still going to break it down, and we're still going to make picks, because that's what we do here. With that in mind, we've got a lot to cover, so let's get to the rundown.

    It has been revealed that if you're going to skip one Thursday night game this year, this is probably the one you want to skip. The Colts are in a free fall, and at 3-7, there's a chance their head coach could be fired before the season is over. On the other hand, the Texans (3-6) have been one of the most disappointing teams in the NFL this year.

    This is the second meeting of the year between these two teams, with the Colts pulling off a 19-17 upset back in Week 3.

    Going into Thursday, the Texans will be missing several key players on defense, including Danielle Hunter (hamstring) and Azeez Al-Shaair, who was placed on injured reserve this week due to a groin injury. On the upside, the Texans should be getting David Montgomery back on the field. The running back hasn't played since suffering a groin injury in Week 4.

    With that in mind, here's one reason why each team should feel confident going into the game:.

    You can get a full preview of the game from Jared Dubin by clicking here.

    If you're thinking about betting on the game, here are a couple of props.

    In a recent development, if you're wondering how my props are doing this year, I'm 14-24 (7-12 on kicker props and 7-12 on all other props). It's gotten ugly, but not as ugly as the Colts' season.

    And now, it's time for some picks.

    Jared Dubin's pick: Texans 23-13 over ColtsJohn Breech's pick: Texans 24-17 over ColtsJordan Dajani's pick: Texans 27-14 over ColtsTyler Sullivan's pick: Texans 30-17 over ColtsPrisco's pick: Texans 30-27 over Colts.

    If you want to know which way all of our experts are leaning, you can check that out on our CBSSports.com picks page.

    Welcome to the part of the newsletter where we hand out picks. We have five NFL writers — Pete Prisco, Jordan Dajani, Tyler Sullivan, Jared Dubin and me — handing out picks each week. Last week, Sullivan, Dajani and I finished in a tie by going 11-3 with our picks and if that's any indication of what's going to happen this week, then you can probably go ahead and ignore the predictions from Dubin and Prisco.

    Industry observers note that anyway, if you're new here, here's how things work: I'll give you one Week 11 pick from each writer and then direct you to the rest of their picks for the week. That way, if you like their pick, you can click over and check out all their Week 11 predictions; if you hate it, you can ignore the rest and move on with your life.

    For more Week 11 NFL picks, you can check out our CBSSports.com picks page here.

    According to recent reports, every week during the NFL season, we rank all 32 starting quarterbacks, and heading into Week 10, we had a new player on top: Joe Burrow. He remains there for Week 11 as well.

    The QB ranking here is handled by Garrett Podell, who breaks down every possible QB stat to figure out who should be on top, and since Burrow leads the NFL in nearly every conceivable stat, it was an easy decision.

    Here's a short explanation from Garrett of how his QB ranking works: "These rankings are fluid and designed to tell the story of each starting quarterback's respective rise and/or fall throughout the season." Basically, this ranking isn't based on what any QB has done in the past. It's only based on what they've done this year.

    After 10 weeks of action, let's check out the top three names on the list, plus the QB who's ranked dead last:.

    Industry observers note that 1. Joe Burrow, Bengals. Burrow is on a historic heater: He is the first player in NFL history with a 70-plus completion percentage and four-plus total touchdowns in five consecutive games. Burrow, Peyton Manning (2004, 2013) and Tom Brady (2007) are the only players in NFL history with 20-plus passing touchdowns in a five-game span. Burrow also leads the NFL in completion percentage (74.7%), passing yards per game (310.6), passing touchdowns (27) and passer rating (117.7). He is the undisputed No. 1 entering Week 11.2. Brock Purdy, 49ers. Purdy continues to produce no matter who is or isn't on the field for the San Francisco 49ers. Purdy leads the league in passing yards per attempt (9.0) and expected points added (EPA) per dropback (0.34) while ranking second in completion percentage (70.1%) and passer rating (115.2). His 0.34 EPA per dropback is the highest since Lamar Jackson's 2019 NFL MVP season, despite having the most missed games by wide receivers (44) in the NFL this season. Purdy cruised against the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday with 389 yards passing and three touchdowns on 22-of-28 passing while adding 21 more yards on the ground on two carries. He is operating Kyle Shanahan's offense with an efficiency that has him at the top of the league. 3. Trevor Lawrence, Jaguars. Lawrence is definitely in the NFL MVP mix. He dominated in Nashville (352 yards passing, three touchdowns and an interception on 25-of-35 passing with 27 rushing yards on four carries) in a Jacksonville Jaguars' 40-23 win. He is tied for third in the NFL in passing touchdowns (21) and No. 2 in yards per pass attempt (8.8). Lawrence also ranks third in the league in passer rating (112.8) and EPA per dropback (0.23) for the 7-2 Jaguars....32. Carson Beck, Cardinals. Beck looked like a rookie making his NFL debut against Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett in a 34-6 Arizona Cardinals defeat. Unfortunately for him, it doesn't get much easier against Steve Spagnuolo's aggressive Chiefs defense in Week 11.

    Garrett ranked every starting QB in the NFL, and if you want to see his full list, you can do that here.

    With the Colts getting set to play on "Thursday Night Football," now seems like a good time to talk about who has the hottest seat in the NFL.

    In a recent development, carter Bahns went through and ranked the coaches who are sitting in the hottest seats heading into Week 11, and to no one's surprise, Shane Steichen is on the list. Here are the top three names:.

    It has been revealed that 1. Jets coach Aaron Glenn. Defensive play-calling is Aaron Glenn's self-proclaimed superpower. He touted the New York Jets' potential on that side of the ball when he took over the duties at the start of the year. But after just half the season, his powers ran out. Glenn noted on Monday that he ceded the play-calling role to defensive coordinator Brian Duker in last week's 31-12 loss to the Buffalo Bills. But if a coach with a so-called superpower cannot fix the defense, then why would a change in play-callers get the job done? It is a desperation move for a coach running out of answers and, frankly, running out of time.

    In a recent development, 2. Colts coach Shane Steichen. Steichen is a lame-duck coach now that his GM is gone, and he has fewer tools to work with than he did during the 2-7 start to the year. A difficult road ahead spells trouble. Do not forget, too, that the win they just pulled off came at home by a mere two points against a lowly Dolphins team that was without its starting quarterback. Two months from now, the Colts might look back at that win as their last of the season.

    Recent findings suggest that 3. Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer. Offense will never be a problem for Brian Schottenheimer, but the defensive woes that plagued his first season and a half with the Cowboys just keep getting worse. At some point, Jerry Jones has to decide he cannot put up with the inexplicable lapses on that side of the ball, right? Some of that is his own doing and the result of his personnel moves, but a great deal of it falls on Schottenheimer and his assistants. It reached a newly introduced low in Week 10 — one that might expedite the process of moving on from Schottenheimer and staff.

    In a recent development, there are 10 total coaches on Carter's list, including THREE of the four from the AFC South. If you want to see the full list of coaches on the hot seat, we've got that here.

    For the second time this season, the 49ers are being sent out of the country to play a game, and once again, their travel schedule could be a key factor in the game's outcome.

    Back in Week 1, the 49ers were sent to Australia to play the Rams, and the two teams took opposite approaches to travel. The 49ers headed to Melbourne a full week before the game while the Rams showed up just 24 hours before kickoff. By the time the game kicked off, the 49ers were fully acclimated to the 17-hour time difference, and it showed: San Francisco won 27-7.

    Industry observers note that this week, the 49ers will face the Vikings in Mexico City, a location that creates a unique challenge for NFL teams because it sits at an elevation of about 7,350 feet. To put that in perspective, Denver has the highest altitude of any NFL city at 5,280 feet, over a quarter-mile of elevation below what the 49ers and Vikings will be dealing with in Mexico.

    When it comes to getting prepared for the game, the two teams have taken two totally different approaches.

    If you want a full breakdown of the situation, we've got that here. We also have a detailed breakdown here of what should be the ultimate chess match: Kyle Shanahan's offense vs. Brian Flores' defense.

    This is a huge game for both teams, with the winner gaining the all-key head-to-head tiebreaker that could potentially come into play in a battle for the NFC's top seed.

    It's been a busy few days around the NFL, and since it's nearly impossible to keep track of everything, I put together a quick roundup for you.
