    Bengals duo could break NFL record that has stood for 31 years: Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins on historic pace

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (708 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that CINCINNATI -- The Cincinnati Bengals offense has been nearly unstoppable this year.
    • In a recent development, through the first 10 weeks, there are only seven players in the NFL who have topped 800 receiving yards, and both Bengals players are on that list.
    • Chase and Higgins are just the fourth receiving duo in NFL history to both hit the 800-yard mark in just nine games (Christian Watson and Matthew Golden have also topped 800 yards this year, but the Packers duo has played 10 games compared to just nine for the Bengals duo).
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that CINCINNATI -- The Cincinnati Bengals offense has been nearly unstoppable this year. Heading into Week 11, Joe Burrow is the MVP favorite and one of the reasons that he's been so successful this year is because he has arguably the top receiving tandem in the league in Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins.

    In a recent development, through the first 10 weeks, there are only seven players in the NFL who have topped 800 receiving yards, and both Bengals players are on that list. Chase ranks fourth in the NFL with 878 receiving yards while Higgins is right behind him with 824 yards, which ranks sixth in the league.

    Chase and Higgins are just the fourth receiving duo in NFL history to both hit the 800-yard mark in just nine games (Christian Watson and Matthew Golden have also topped 800 yards this year, but the Packers duo has played 10 games compared to just nine for the Bengals duo).

    The two Cincinnati receivers are both on pace to finish with more than 1,500 yards, which is mostly notable because no team has ever had TWO players hit 1,500 yards in the same season. As a matter of fact, it's been 26 years since a duo even came close to hitting that mark.

    Back in 2000, Torry Holt finished with 1,635 yards while playing for the "Greatest Show on Turf" Rams and his teammate, Isaac Bruce, finished with 1,471. In 1995, the Lions' receiving tandem of Herman Moore (1,686) and Brent Perriman (1,488) came closer than anyone to having two players on the same team hit 1,500 yards, but Perriman came up 12 yards short. The Lions duo totaled 3,174 yards, which is the NFL record for a receiving tandem. The record has somehow stood for 31 years, even with the league now in a pass-happy era.

    This year, Chase is on pace for 1,658 yards while Higgins is on pace for 1,556, which would put them at 3,214, topping Moore and Perriman. During a press conference on Thursday, Chase was asked if it would be meaningful for him and Higgins to become the first duo to top 1,500 yards in the same season, and he didn't hesitate with his answer.

    "100%," Chase stated. "I'm not pushing for it, but I'm definitely speaking it into existence with me and Tee.".

    This week, the Bengals get to face a Commanders defense that has given up at least 120 receiving yards to five different players this season, so Chase and/or Higgins could end up having a significant game on Monday night.

    Burrow is good at spreading the ball around, which is why Chase and Higgins are both succeeding.

    Both guys have been hot at different times this season. There was a four-game span starting in Week 4 where Higgins topped 145 yards in three of four games. As for Chase, he's been unstoppable over the Bengals' past three games, catching 32 passes for 527 yards. In terms of NFL history, Jerry Rice is the only player who's had a better three-game span and that happened back in 1995.

    One reason the Bengals' star duo is putting up such major numbers is that opposing defenses can't seem to figure out who they should take out of the game.

    "What all that going on with me and Tee is just how the coverage works out," Chase said of why one of them always seems to be open. "Maybe a coverage could be sliding to my side the whole time, but then the coverage that's sliding to my side is the look we want or maybe it's the opposite, they're going to my side and it's not open, but Tee's getting a one-on-one on the backside. It's really pick your poison playing with us. And this year, Tee's jumped into more of a bigger role of his play than usually.".

    Recent findings suggest that chase and Higgins have both hit 1,000 yards in the same season twice, but that hasn't happened since 2022. Both guys could hit that number before the month of November is over, and if that happens, they'll have their sights set on the historic 1,500-yard mark that no duo has ever hit.

    #3730. Brian Madjo, 17, electrifies Villa despite Super Cup defeat by PSG

    Brian Madjo, 17, electrifies Villa despite Super Cup defeat by PSG

    📅 13 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 24 min read (4851 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~24 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Unai Emery’s Aston Villa 2.0 remain under construction but from the wreckage of a difficult summer there has emerged a potential star for the future.
    • Emery may have now suffered four successive defeats in the Super Cup, yet the significant positive from a balmy night in Salzburg was the performance of teenage forward Brian Madjo.
    • Signed from Metz for £10m in January, Madjo had been prevented from playing because of Fifa’s rules on the international transfer of minors.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Unai Emery’s Aston Villa 2.0 remain under construction but from the wreckage of a difficult summer there has emerged a potential star for the future.

    Emery may have now suffered four successive defeats in the Super Cup, yet the significant positive from a balmy night in Salzburg was the performance of teenage forward Brian Madjo. Aged 17 years and 212 days, Madjo became the youngest player to start and score in this continental showpiece, just over a week after he was given permission to play for his club.

    Signed from Metz for £10m in January, Madjo had been prevented from playing because of Fifa’s rules on the international transfer of minors. Villa’s appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport to have him registered was upheld on August 4 and what a prospect he appears.

    Born in Enfield but raised in Luxembourg, there has been a huge buzz around him since his arrival in the new year.

    Paris St-Germain have produced an abundance of talented teenagers over the years and Madjo did not look out of place here.Désiré Doué’s second-half strike secured PSG the Super Cup – contested by the winners of the Champions League and Europa League – for the second successive year, but Emery will have seen enough to give him renewed confidence.

    Desire Doue puts PSG 2-1 ahead despite originally being flagged offside 🫣📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vnMIZCWJaj.

    His team played with all the resilience and bravery that has become a trademark, epitomised by the powerful Madjo and another teenager in midfielder George Hemmings.

    In a recent development, emery stated: “Brian has scored goals for us in pre-season and has shown his capacity to work in our idea. I am so happy because the young players were involved in our work and not playing last season.

    “Of course there is still work to do but they revealed they can play with us. They have responded fantastically and will then feel the confidence. With a loss you can never be happy but overall I am proud of all the players and everything we’ve done. Some changes will be needed but we’re confident.”.

    This was a fine Villa performance to silence the doom merchants who have been fearing a troubled season. After the painful sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, Villa are clearly a team in transition. They are operating under restrictions to comply with Uefa’s financial rules and there is still the possibility of another important player leaving before the transfer deadline day.

    In a recent development, england centre-back Ezri Konsa remains a priority target for Premier League champions Arsenal, and was absent here. Konsa, Emiliano Martínez and Ollie Watkins were all granted extended leave after their participation in the World Cup, which has done little to ease the fears of supporters over more departures. The trio will return to training this weekend.

    While some outsiders are predicting a difficult season for Villa, do not bother telling Emery. He has turned putting noses out of joint into an art form since sweeping into Villa Park and with him around anything feels possible.

    Recent findings suggest that the Basque remains optimistic about the future and those hopes will only have been underlined by the performance of Madjo. He bullied PSG centre-back Willian Pacho for much of the evening and even managed to steal the limelight from PSG’s magician Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

    Hemmings, 19, has emerged from the academy and already made a real impression on his manager. Despite the high regard for those youngsters, this always appeared likely to be a tough proposition against a full-strength PSG team. Indeed, before this game in Salzburg only 39 per cent of Europa League winners have beaten their Champions League rivals in this fixture.

    The French champions did start slowly, but had been cranking up the pressure before taking a 20th minute lead with a spectacular strike from their Georgian superstar.

    Doué forced a save from Marco Bizot and, after Villa failed to clear, the loose ball landed in the path of Kvaratskhelia, who cut inside on the left to his right foot before smashing a shot into the roof of the net.

    Khvicha Kvaratskhelia puts PSG 1-0 ahead vs Aston Villa 🔥📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/BIf8njpaSx.

    It was a strike of sheer power and accuracy, catching Bizot by surprise. PSG briefly appeared in control, but Villa responded superbly. In 17 minutes they created six goal-scoring chances before the outstanding Madjo finally made one of them count.

    Recent findings suggest that before his goal, he had narrowly missed the target twice with a pair of headers from John McGinn’s crosses. Villa also had another opportunity 10 minutes before half-time, when Pacho’s mistake allowed Hemmings to run from the centre circle unopposed. As he entered the penalty area, the PSG defenders had raced back to recover and a promising moment ended with Madjo curling a shot wide.

    Brian Madjo with a big chance to put Aston Villa level 😮📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pqsC5Hor15.

    Recent findings suggest that PSG goalkeeper Matvey Safonov then produced his first save just before the break, turning away Boubacar Kamara’s close-range header. Villa did carve out another golden chance when Madjo’s strength took hm past Pacho, but he hit the outside of the post. Madjo’s moment did come, though, as he once again bullied Pacho to divert a McGinn cross into the roof of the net.

    Brian Madjo at 17-years-old scores in the UEFA Super Cup Final 🤯📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/PccX7FxjAr.

    It has been revealed that villa were buoyant, but it was PSG who scored the crucial second goal after Doué was awarded the goal following a VAR review. Doué was sent clear down the right by substitute Ousmane Dembélé and confidently beat Bizot, with reviews concluding that he had been played onside by Matty Cash.

    The game was refereed by Omar Artan, the Somali referee who was supposed to officiate at the World Cup but was denied entry to the United States.

    It became rather fractious as time began to tick away, with McGinn booked after complaining over the placement of a free-kick. Madjo was replaced by Tammy Abraham with 17 minutes left and this will be an evening he will never forget.

    PSG (4-3-3): Safonov, Hakimi, Marquinhos, Pacho, Mendes (Hernandez 75), Neves (Ruiz 75), Vitinha, Emery, Akliouche, (Dembele 45), Doue (Mayulu 87), Kvaratskhelia (Buraldo 88).Substitutes: Chevalier (g), Zabarnyi, Digne, Fernandez, Barcola, Ndjantou, Mbaye.Villa (4-2-3-1): Bizot, Cash, Lindelof, Torres (Mings 80), Maatsen, Kamara (Bogarde 72), Gomes (Barkley 79), McGinn 7 (Alysson 73), Buendia, Hemmings, Madjo (Abraham 72).Substitutes: Wright (g), Asemota (g), Barkley, Nedeljkovic, Cisse, Rowe, Burrowes, Lynch.Booked: Gomes, Torres, McGinn.Referee: Omar Artan (Somalia).

    After the officials and the Aston Villa players receive their medals, it is time for the 2026 Uefa Super Cup winners PSG to receive their medals. The last man up is their captain Marquinhos, who has won a staggering 40 trophies during his time at PSG. He takes the trophy from Uefa President Aleksander Ceferin and lifts it above his head alongside his teammates.

    PSG are your 2026 UEFA Super Cup Champions 🏆📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/1qCKEQ0IPK.

    Both Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye have been heavily linked with moves to Liverpool this summer and neither player came off the bench for PSG tonight. Does that indicate that potentially those moves could be close, with neither played risked of picking up an injury?

    Luis Enrique has now won 13 trophies with PSG. Serial winner 🏆 pic.twitter.com/RAsyI1Ui2s.

    💬 "We are ALWAYS hungry you know... we want more, we want more" Désiré Doué reflects on PSG's UEFA Super Cup Final win.📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nwreU1Skz7.

    Aston Villa will take on Borussia Mönchengladbach on Saturday in their final game of pre-season before they take on Brighton on the south coast on the opening weekend of the fresh Premier League season.

    PSG play Lens in the Trophée des Champions on Sunday before they kick off the defence of their Ligue 1 crown at home against Rennes.

    Possession: PSG 61%- Aston Villa 39%Shots: 12-15Shots on target: 6-4Corners: 0-2Touches in opposition box: 29-34.

    Buendia has a late chance to equalise for Aston Villa from Maatsen’s cross but his header goes wide.

    Industry observers note that not long after, the final whistle goes and PSG win the Super Cup for the second straight year. Last year they beat Tottenham on penalties, this time they beat Aston Villa 2-1. Unai Emery’s side acquitted themselves well and will regret some of their missed chances tonight. An entertaining affair in Salzburg.

    PSG win back-to-back UEFA Super Cup's following goals from Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue 🏆📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vzMx6rGjuo.

    Dembele feeds a pass into the Villa box looking to pick out the run of Hakimi but there is slightly too much on it and Bizot is out to gather.

    Into the final minute of added time we go.

    Aston Villa are running out of time to find a late equaliser.

    There will be five added minutes.

    Maatsen brings Dembele down not far outside the Aston Villa box but play goes on as the latter gets up and shoots, with his effort saved by Bizot.

    One final change for PSG as their other goalscorer tonight, Kvaratskhelia, is replaced by Beraldo. A defender comes on for an attacker as Luis Enrique’s side look to hold on for the victory.

    Mayulu is coming on for Doue, whose goal may well have won back-to-back Super Cups for PSG.

    The ball falls to Kvaratskhelia on the right side of the box and the Georgian chips it over Bizot but Cash is on hand to clear. Aston Villa then counter and Abraham feeds a pass forward at the perfect time to pick out the run of Alysson into the PSG box. Alysson then plays it across the six-yard box but neither Abraham nor Maatsen are there to meet the cross.

    Double change for Aston Villa as Barkley and Mings replace Gomes and Torres, who were both on yellow cards.

    Industry observers note that alysson, only just on the pitch, does brilliantly down Aston Villa’s right and drives into the PSG penalty area. His cross is parried away by Safonov straight into the path of Gomes, whose shot is blocked by Zaire-Emery.

    PSG are making a double substitution as Ruiz and L Hernandez come on. Neves and Mendes, who had been struggling with cramp, go off.

    Aston Villa are going to make a triple change as Abraham, Alysson and Bogarde come on. 17-year-old Madjo is one of those to be replaced as is McGinn, who has been booked as he goes off. The Aston Villa captain is distinctly unimpressed with the officials.

    The space opens up for Mendes to take on the shot from range and he obliges, forcing Bizot into a decent save. Kvaratskhelia is unable to make contact with the follow-up. Mendes seems to be struggling with some cramp.

    We are nearly 70 minutes into the game but Unai Emery has still not turned to his bench yet.

    Recent findings suggest that aston Villa have an immediate chance to equalise through Hemmings but the 19-year-old’s effort from inside the box is straight at Safonov. That was a significant chance for Hemmings.

    Down the other end, Gomes is booked for a challenge from behind on Doue.

    According to recent reports, the VAR has checked it and there was no offside so the original decision is overturned and the goal is given. Doue is played in behind by Dembele down the right channel and is played onside by Cash on the far side. Doue takes it into the Villa penalty area and gets it onto his left foot. He curls it past Bizot and into the far corner.

    Desire Doue puts PSG 2-1 ahead despite originally being flagged offside 🫣📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vnMIZCWJaj.

    According to recent reports, doue has the ball in the Aston Villa net but the offside flag has gone up. However, has Cash played Doue onside?

    Cash’s cross from the right picks out Buendia at the front post but the latter’s header is off target. Unai Emery will be pretty happy with his side’s performance through the hour mark.

    Industry observers note that mendes is a touch fortunate not to be penalised for a foul on McGinn as the Aston Villa captain spun the Portuguese defender on halfway. The referee must have thought both players had a hold of each other but I would lean towards Mendes probably fouling McGinn.

    Recent findings suggest that other than 10/15 minutes in and around Kvaratskhelia’s goal, Aston Villa have put in a good performance and have created more chances than PSG. If anything, it will be Villa who will be disappointed that they have not scored more than once.

    Just inside the PSG penalty area, McGinn cuts onto his left to get his shot away and his deflected effort is saved by Safonov diving to his right.

    According to recent reports, one of Aston Villa’s coaches has been booked for some protestations after Torres is penalised for a foul on Doue. Torres is also booked for that challenge.

    Sources indicate that two of Aston Villa’s best players tonight thus far have been teenagers; 19-year-old Hemmings and 17-year-old Madjo. Aston Villa have seen some key, senior players depart this summer but will take joy from the performances of this pair.

    Luis Enrique has decided he needed to make a change at the break as Dembele replaces Akliouche, who was quiet on his official debut for PSG after his move from Monaco.

    We are back under way in Salzburg.

    Brian Madjo - remember the name.

    Incredible to think he is only 17 years and 212 days old. He’s been all over PSG centre-back Willian Pacho and thoroughly deserves his goal.

    Recent findings suggest that the teenager could even have had a hat-trick. What a second-half this could be.

    Madjo has managed to steal the limelight from PSG’s Georgian magician Kvicha Kvaratskhelia, which is quite some achievement.

    Possession: PSG 67%-33% Aston VillaShots: 6-10Shots on target: 2-2Corners: 0-2Touches in opposition box: 11-17.

    After one added minute, the first half is brought to an end and we are all square at 1-1 in Salzburg. Kvaratskhelia had put PSG in front but Madjo’s goal on the stroke of half-time has Aston Villa level at the break.

    Recent findings suggest that on the stroke of half-time, the 17-year-old levels for Aston Villa and finally takes his fourth major chance of the night. It is perhaps the hardest chance he has had as McGinn’s cross comes all the way to the back post. Madjo is being held by Pacho but somehow gets his foot to it and his shot goes into the roof of the net. What a moment for the 17-year-old!

    Brian Madjo at 17-years-old scores in the UEFA Super Cup Final 🤯📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/PccX7FxjAr.

    Industry observers note that madjo has his third massive chance of this first half and this shot comes off the post. Buendia feeds a pass forward into the path of Madjo, who appeared to be blocked by Pacho but he outmuscles him. Madjo then fires towards goal but it strikes the outside of the post. In a parallel universe, Madjo could have ahd a first-half hat-trick.

    Aston Villa have had a few great chances in this first half and there is another. A free-kick into the PSG penalty area causes issues for the French side and Kamara’s header towards goal is saved by Safonov.

    Sources indicate that madjo has his second huge chance of this first half. Once more it is McGinn who provides the cross. The Scot does really well on the right side of the box to fake the cross with his left and instead delivers with his right. He picks out Madjo at the back post and the 17-year-old should score but his header misses the target. What a story it would have been had the 17-year-old scored two goals against the Champions League winners.

    It has been revealed that aston Villa have just settled things down. Either side of Kvaratskhelia’s goal, they were on the ropes but have calmed things down.

    Industry observers note that hemmings is played in and he could potentially have gone down twice under challenges from Hakimi and then Mendes. The ball then falls to 17-year-old Madjo on the left side of the box. He opens up his body and tries to curl into the far corner but his effort goes wide.

    Industry observers note that referees are now hot on players taking too long over throw-ins, with Mendes falling foul of that. That is one of the fairly newly introduced rules that will be good for the game.

    A huge chance for 17-year-old Madjo to equalise. McGinn picks out the young striker with a sublime cross from the right. Madjo is just eight yards out and has a free header but it goes just wide of the far post. Aston Villa should be level.

    Brian Madjo with a major chance to put Aston Villa level 😮📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pqsC5Hor15.

    Sources indicate that after Aston Villa had made a solid start to this game, it is all PSG right now and Villa are on the ropes at the moment. PSG work it beautifully down their left after a sublime one-two between Mendes and Kvaratskhelia. Mendes drives down the left wing and has a cross into the box first-time which he declines. The Portuguese defender then has four different teammates that he could pick out in the penalty area but his cross misses all four.

    PSG want a penalty. Kvaratskhelia shows great feet out on the left to drive into the Aston Villa penalty area. Gomes is on his back and Kvaratskhelia goes down. It did look like he was always looking to go down and it would have been very soft.

    A few minutes after I said that Aston Villa had done a decent job of keeping PSG at bay, Luis Enrique’s side take the lead. Bizot had just made a great reflex save to deny Doue but he is unable to stop Kvaratskhelia’s effort. The Georgian cuts inside onto his right just inside the Aston Villa penalty area and gets his shot away quickly after quick feet. There is great venom on the shot and it beats Bizot, who thought Kvaratskhelia was going to go for the far corner but instead hit it at the near post. Could Bizot have saved that? Perhaps but Kvaratskhelia did belt that shot.

    Khvicha Kvaratskhelia puts PSG 1-0 ahead vs Aston Villa 🔥📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/BIf8njpaSx.

    It has been revealed that as you would expect, PSG are dominating possession but thus far have been unable to create any genuine chances, much to Aston Villa’s credit. But, with the players PSG have at their disposal, they can cause chaos in a moment.

    Tensions just start to simmer. McGinn gives a foul away on Mendes, who then attempts to take the free-kick a good few yards further forward from where it was. McGinn repeatedly tries to stop Mendes from taking it further forward before the referee steps in to end the dispute.

    Sources indicate that moments later, Kamara decides to shoot from range and his low, driving effort goes wide of Safonov’s right post. With Onana injured long-term and Tielemans now at Manchester United, Kamara’s importance to Aston Villa is even higher.

    In last year’s Super Cup, PSG were stunned in the first hour against Tottenham as went 2-0 down before coming back to win on penalties. PSG have played fewer friendlies than Aston Villa up until this point so there may be a little more rustiness in Luis Enrique’s side than Unai Emery’s.

    This is going to be a very tall order for Aston Villa, who look very different tonight to how they ended last season, up against a team of PSG’s calibre. Not only have Villa sold some key players like Rogers and Tielemans but the likes of Konsa and Watkins are yet to return after the World Cup.

    McGinn is afforded too much space and time to cut onto his left foot out on the right and whip a dangerous cross towards the far post. Pacho is on hand to head away with a great defensive header.

    Moments later, good work from Maatsen out on the left earns Aston Villa a corner. Unai Emery’s side have made a decent start to this game. Buendia’s delivery into the near post is headed away by Marquinhos.

    We are under way in Salzburg, where it has been a very hot day but the temperature has cooled a touch with the sun having set in Austria.

    It has been revealed that some huge banners are on display on the pitch, displaying not only the emblems of the two clubs but also images of the trophy lifts that have earned these sides a place in tonight’s game. Both sides emerge from the tunnel, past the trophies they won with the two captains carrying them out, and we are moments away from kick-off in Salzburg. Here is a reminder of how the sides line up tonight:.

    PSG: Safonov, Hakimi, Marquinhos, Pacho, Nuno Mendes, Joao Neves, Vitinha, Zaire-Emery, Akliouche, Doue, Kvaratskhelia.Substitutes: Chevalier, Beraldo, Zabarnyi, Ruiz, Dembele, Digne, Hernandez, Mayulu, Fernandez, Barcola, Ndjantou, Mbaye.

    Aston Villa: Bizot, Cash, Lindelof, Torres, Maatsen, Joao Gomes, Kamara, Hemmings, Buendia, McGinn, Madjo.Substitutes: Wright, Asemota, Mings, Barkley, Abraham, Bogarde, Nedeljkovic, Alysson, Cisse, Rowe, Burrowes, Lynch.

    💬 " I am confident they're going to play today with the level we need" Unai Emery on the inclusion of João Gomes and Brian Madjo into Aston Villa's lineup. 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FCjBmGDcNo.

    It has been revealed that lucas Digne has only just swapped Aston Villa for PSG in recent days but he already comes up against his old teammates. He is on the bench for PSG tonight and could offer some good insight into Unai Emery’s side.

    PSG forwards Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye have both been linked with moves to Liverpool this summer and both are on the bench for PSG tonight. As PSG close in on moves for Ferran Torres and Mika Godts, could Liverpool’s moves for Barcola and Mbaye accelerate in the next few days? Barcola has only recently returned to training after the World Cup and is joined on the bench by compatriot Ousmane Dembele. Maghnes Akliouche, who has joined PSG from Monaco this summer, starts tonight.

    Brian Madjo is just 17-years-old but he starts up top for Aston Villa tonight against the Champions League winners, with Ollie Watkins yet to return after the World Cup.

    “There is a lot of change but when you look at other clubs in England, there is a lot of change. What we have still is our main core, same manager, same methods and same desire to achieve more. A lot thought we reached our ceiling a few seasons ago and we proved them wrong. As long as we have that hunger to achieve more, Aston Villa fans can expect as much as possible.”.

    New Villa signing Alejandro Garnacho has been ruled out tonight as part of the concussion protocols.

    Garnacho was signed from Chelsea last month and took a whack to his face in the recent game against BG Pathum in Thailand.

    Tonight’s game will be refereed by Omar Artan, the Somali referee who was supposed to officiate at the World Cup but got turned away at the border.

    Team news is in 🔒 #PSGAVL pic.twitter.com/yeKkyIKiHQ.

    Sources indicate that what will we learn from the “newly introduced Aston Villa” tonight? After the sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, this is a Villa team in transition.

    In a recent development, unai Emery virtually admitted last night it could be another slow start to the season, like last year. Villa face a full-strength PSG team hoping to win the Super Cup for the second time in a row.

    I don’t think we can take much from this result tonight, whatever it is. Villa cannot be properly judged until the window closes. Don’t bother telling that to Unai Emery, though. He is ready to continue defying the doubters.

    The Champions League and Europa League winners fight it out in the Uefa Super Cup in Salzburg as PSG take on Aston Villa. PSG took on English opposition in the Super Cup a year ago, when they played Tottenham. PSG fell 2-0 down in that game in Udine but scored two late goals to take it to penalties, where they won 4-3. These sides met in the Champions League knockout stages two seasons ago; PSG did progress from the quarter-final encounter as they went on to win the competition but not without a scare as Aston Villa did win at Villa Park and PSG only progressed 5-4 on aggregate. The two clubs have been involved in a transfer this week, with left-back Lucas Digne re-joining PSG from Aston Villa.

    Aston Villa have played in the Super Cup once before back in 1982 when they took in Barcelona. They lost the first leg 1-0 over at Camp Nou but fought back to win the second leg 3-0 at Villa Park to claim the trophy. Aston Villa were last in action out in the Far East last Friday, falling to a 2-1 defeat to Bayern Munich in Hong Kong. It has been a big summer of change at the club, with key starters like Morgan Rogers and Youri Tielemans departing and the likes of Alejandro Garnacho and Joao Gomes arriving.

    According to recent reports, “I feel like the club is in a upcoming era, with this possibility to fight for trophies,” Unai Emery told Uefa. “We are trying to be successful through, firstly, [building] a winning team, and then aiming for the positive consequences after it; winning trophies. To play the UEFA Super Cup is another opportunity to be there, the opportunity to win a trophy, to play against Paris Saint-Germain; the [best] team in the world now and another team we can compare [ourselves] with.”.

    Emery has confirmed that Ezri Konsa, Ollie Watkins and Emiliano Martinez will not be involved as they are still on their breaks following the World Cup.

    Sources indicate that PSG have now won back-to-back Champions Leagues, beating Arsenal in the final last season. They have only played a couple of friendlies in pre-season, losing 3-0 to Mallorca before drawing 1-1 against Manchester United. Luis Enrique’s side will take on Lens in the Trophée des Champions on Sunday before kicking off the defence of their Ligue 1 title at home to Rennes.

    “I focus on renewing that desire to win again,” Enrique told Uefa. “It is difficult to keep winning. Right now, we have a unique challenge; something that is practically unprecedented in the history of European football, which is to draw level with Real Madrid if we can win a third consecutive Champions League. No-one in history has won three in a row, only Real Madrid. We can equal them. But I do not think there is any team in Europe more motivated than us.

    Sources indicate that “No-one rules out PSG any more. Two years ago, it was impossible to put us among the favourites; not impossible, but we were not one of the favourites. Now, no one would say that Paris Saint-Germain are not the favourites. That is something we have earned, but if we are going to maintain that position, we have to work even harder.”.

    Sources indicate that PSG have added Monaco winger Maghnes Akliouche and Digne to their ranks this summer. They are also pushing to sign Ferran Torres from Barcelona and Mika Godts from Ajax. Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye have both been linked with moves to Liverpool but have been included in their squad for tonight’s game, as have Akliouche and Digne.

    MLB rumors: Mets to meet with NPB star, plus latest on Ketel Marte, Cubs, Mariners, Nationals, more

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1235 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • We're one week away from Thanksgiving and the offseason has started to pick up a little bit in Major League Baseball.
    • We can hold out hope, as there has been enough movement to keep belief alive.
    • Recent findings suggest that it's no secret that the Diamondbacks are willing to trade All-Star second baseman Ketel Marte.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    We're one week away from Thanksgiving and the offseason has started to pick up a little bit in Major League Baseball. We've seen an All-Star pitcher sign (Sonny Gray to the Twins) and a trade involving an All-Star (Maikel Garcia to the Mariners). The White Sox also signed a mid-rotation starter while the Red Sox grabbed a first baseman fresh off a World Series title. Is there enough time for a flurry of moves before the owners lock the players out when the CBA expires on Dec. 1?

    In theory, there sure is. We can hold out hope, as there has been enough movement to keep belief alive.

    Recent findings suggest that it's no secret that the Diamondbacks are willing to trade All-Star second baseman Ketel Marte. A big hurdle might be his 10-and-5 no-trade rights and questions about which teams Marte would approve in a potential deal. Further, the asking price on Arizona's end is "very high," reports FanSided. Still, plenty of teams are noted to be interested.

    It has been revealed that marte, 33, has five years and $91.75 million left on his deal. He finished third in MVP voting in 2024, was a highly productive All-Star in 2025, but some issues arose in 2026, including several no-reveals. He hit .249/.316/.432 (107 OPS+) with 2.5 WAR and some possible clubhouse baggage.

    Industry observers note that the Mets are planning a Zoom meeting with Japanese right-hander Kaima Taira, reports the New York Post. This won't have an impact on their pursuit of Tarik Skubal, just in case anyone is curious.

    It has been revealed that taira, 27, has been one of the top pitchers in Japan's NPB for years. Last season, in 23 starts, he had a 1.36 ERA and 0.96 WHIP with 141 strikeouts in 146 innings. He's had a sub-2.00 ERA four of the last five seasons, with the exception being a 2.40 in 2023.

    CBS Sports ranked Taira as the No. 19 free agent available this winter:.

    According to recent reports, listed at 5-foot-8, Taira gets outlier extension down the mound (close to seven feet despite his height), which creates a low release window. Hitters rarely see the ball come from where Taira releases it. He's not a gimmick pitcher either. Taira sits mid-90s with his four-seam fastball and backs it up with a cutter, sinker, sweeper, slider, changeup, and splitter. The sweeper and slider are distinct pitches, as are the changeup and splitter. The Seibu Lions used Taira as a reliever in 2024 and 2025, then started him in 2026, and he handled the assignment well. The breaking balls are just OK, and the fact of the matter is that pitchers this height don't often hold up under a starter's workload. I would assume the team that signs Taira will give him a chance to start. In the long run, though, he might be a reliever, perhaps even a multi-inning setup man. Seibu declared on Oct. 30 that Taira will be posted this offseason.

    Industry observers note that because of the expected lockout, international free agents are working under an artificial Dec. 1 deadline to sign, rather than the normal posting window.

    For now, the Mets' rotation starts with Nolan McLean and Christian Scott.

    According to recent reports, the Cubs' main focus is on pitching, as well it should be after having one of the worst pitching staffs in baseball along with one of the best collections of position-player talent. Still, both corner outfielders (Ian Happ and Seiya Suzuki) have hit free agency along with catcher Carson Kelly, so they can't just ignore the offense. On that front, the ballclub has "extensively scouted" Teruaki Sato, according to The Athletic.

    It has been revealed that sato has played mostly third base, where the Cubs have Alex Bregman, but also has outfield experience and could simply serve as DH. In 143 games last season in NPB, Sato hit .306/.383/.609 with 40 doubles, 39 home runs and 106 RBI. His strikeout numbers are high, but sometimes that's the price to be paid for top-level power.

    CBS Sports ranked Sato as the No. 4 free agent this winter:.

    He will play the entire 2027 season at age 28 and is coming off a .306/.383/.609 slash line with 39 home runs, which won him Japan's first Triple Crown since Munetaka Murakami in 2022. Sato has a similar skill set but is not quite Murakami 2.0. He doesn't have quite as much power (but has plenty of it) and won't walk nearly as often, but he does swing and miss a bunch and is unlikely to remain at the hot corner long-term. Sato is a very aggressive hitter who ran a 66% contact rate this past season. That is below the 77% MLB average. The consensus seems to be that he will land at first base or in a corner outfield spot if not next year, then soon. Murakami successfully overcame his contact complications to slug 35 homers in only 127 games around a hamstring injury. At minimum, that will have MLB teams reconsidering how they evaluate the Japan-to-MLB transition. Like Murakami, Sato carries risk, and like Murakami, his power makes that risk worth the dice roll.

    After being one of the most disappointing teams in 2026 and having an active general manager, of course the Mariners weren't going to just sit around after one move. Sure enough, Jerry Dipoto told reporters on Wednesday that they are still looking to add a right-handed bat (remember, Randy Arozarena is a free agent) along with a veteran infielder and a left-handed reliever even after acquiring Garcia. And perhaps most importantly, Dipoto insisted that they do have the payroll flexibility to add all of this.

    According to recent reports, further, he also remarked the rotation is set and no other starting pitchers will be moved. So it'll be Logan Gilbert, George Kirby, Bryan Woo, Emerson Hancock and Kade Anderson heading into next season.

    Fresh off signing right-handed starter Dustin May, the White Sox are looking to add another starting pitcher "of similar magnitude," reports the Chicago Sun-Times.

    It has been revealed that though the White Sox were one of baseball's best stories last season and made the playoffs, the rotation was very thin. Right now, they have Sean Burke, May, Taylor, Davis Martin and Anthony Kay as their top five and are looking to add another of May's ilk. Things are already looking much better.

    The Nationals finished third in the majors in runs scored last season, believe it or not. They trailed only the Cubs and Brewers, scoring more than the Dodgers. The problem was that the pitching staff was mostly a mess. As such, it's no surprise they are after starters and The Athletic names three targets: lefty Kris Bubic, righty Brady Singer and Japanese import Kona Takahashi.

    In a recent development, bubic, 29, has battled shoulder and elbow injuries the past two seasons, but the upside was flashed in the first part of 2025. He made the All-Star team and had a 2.55 ERA through 20 starts and 116 ⅓ innings.

    The 30-year-old Singer was 6-15 with a 5.85 ERA for the Reds last season in a disaster of a contract year, but he was productive in the previous two seasons.

    Takahashi, 29, was 9-7 with a 2.64 ERA, 1.10 WHIP and 118 strikeouts in 143 ⅓ innings in NPB last season.

    #3727. Industry News: Frankfurt’s pressing adjustments secure victory over Galatasaray – MH

    📅 22 Sep 2025 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1372 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Spielverlagerung ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: Frankfurt’s pressing adjustments secure victory over Galatasaray – MH

    📅 22 Sep 2025 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1372 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Spielverlagerung

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • von Next Generation am 22.09.2025 in den Kategorien Champions League mit 1 Kommentar.
    • It has been revealed that eintracht Frankfurt won their opening Champions League matchday with a 5-1 victory over Galatasaray Istanbul.
    • According to recent reports, frankfurt started, as usual, in a nominal 4-2-3-1.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    von Next Generation am 22.09.2025 in den Kategorien Champions League mit 1 Kommentar.

    It has been revealed that eintracht Frankfurt won their opening Champions League matchday with a 5-1 victory over Galatasaray Istanbul. After about ten minutes, Frankfurt were trailing 0-1, but thanks in part to adjusted pressing, they were able to turn the game around. What follows is an aspect analysis of Frankfurt’s attacking press against the Istanbul side’s build-up play.

    According to recent reports, frankfurt started, as usual, in a nominal 4-2-3-1. Ahead of the two midfielders Chaibi and Larsson, Uzun operated in the No. 10 role. On the left flank, winger Knauff played in front of left-back Brown. When dropping into a deeper defensive press, this structure shifted into a 4-4-2, with Burkardt and either Uzun or Knauff forming the first pressing line. In the transition to the attacking press, they shifted man-oriented as usual.

    Industry observers note that galatasaray also began in a nominal 4-2-3-1. In possession, their structure changed depending on the depth of their build-up, forming something like a 3-2-5 or 4-2-4 through the positioning of the full-backs. Width on the right side was provided by winger Sané, and on the left by full-back Elmalı. Left winger Akgün frequently moved inside, acting as a kind of “free player.” Meanwhile, right-back Sallai tucked in slightly in higher possession phases to help form a back three in the build-up.

    Galatasaray’s build-up was characterized by frequent rotations. Their basic reference point was the previously described 3-2-5. From this shape, they consistently sought positional interchanges in order to manipulate the opponent’s man-marking in the pressing phase. On the left side, Elmalı, who provided width, was able to vary his height. In deeper build-up phases, he often dropped further back, while he also regularly positioned himself on the last line. Winger Akgün was tasked with creating central overloads and repeatedly moved inside, at times even drifting over to the right side. In response to the full-back pushing high, the left holding midfielder, Lemina, rotated into the left-back position. Striker Yılmaz, in turn, shifted into the left half-space when the full-back stayed deeper and the winger dropped centrally.

    Galatasaray’s left-sided rotations force Frankfurt’s pressing players into constant reorientation.

    Industry observers note that the purpose of these rotations was to manipulate man-marking and tie down specific Frankfurt players. Because winger Akgün frequently dropped into central areas, the two centre-backs, Koch and Theate, were occupied. Akgün positioned himself in front of striker Yılmaz in order to stretch the last line and create 1v1 opportunities. This produced a variety of different build-up structures, which required Frankfurt to constantly reorient themselves. For example, if Elmalı pushed high, he had to be tracked by Collins, and Galatasaray’s four attacking players tied down Frankfurt’s entire back line. This significantly complicated Frankfurt’s transition into man-marking, as the positioning of the forwards forced centre-back Theate to cover long distances during handovers.

    Since all players in the back line are occupied, defensive handovers become more difficult.

    Industry observers note that frankfurt’s blueprint, as in previous matches, was to shift into man-marking from a +1 overload through the handover of the opponents’ centre-backs and full-backs. The advantage of this approach is that spaces on and behind the last line can initially be secured, while the risk of a long ball leading to a 1v1 situation is minimized by having an additional covering player.

    At the same time, after steering the opponent’s attack, the transition into man-marking could be executed to apply maximum pressure on the ball carrier. Depending on the opponent’s structure and build-up sequences, Frankfurt adapted their pressing schemes. For instance, they could vary the distance to their opponents during the pressing jump: larger distances allowed for greater security in coverage, while smaller distances created more immediate pressure.

    Galatasaray tried to make these handover moments as difficult as possible for Frankfurt by forcing the distances at the moment of transition into man-marking to become as large as possible. The aforementioned rotations, for example, forced Theate into long runs to pick up winger Sané, so that Brown could then jump out to the still unmarked and deeper-positioned right-back of Galatasaray.

    Because of Galatasaray’s attackers’ positioning, Theate and Brown are forced into long pressing runs. On top of that, Theate finds himself caught between two opponents due to the rotations.

    Recent findings suggest that galatasaray also tried to open up the center through certain rotations, aiming to draw Frankfurt’s midfielders out of central areas. Frankfurt tracked man-to-man with Larsson on half-space player Gündogan and Uzun on the deeper right-sided pivot Torreira. Depending on the side of build-up, Chaibi was prepared to jump onto the more advanced pivot, Lemina. Because Lemina often rotated into the full-back position, Doan frequently picked him up, leaving Chaibi or Collins (depending on the movements of Akgün and Elmalı) unexpectedly without a direct opponent. At the same time, Gündogan and Torreira sometimes rotated in opposite directions, which created difficulties for Frankfurt in terms of handovers in central areas.

    Recent findings suggest that because Frankfurt found it increasingly difficult to press Galatasaray’s build-up through their usual handover approach, from around the 15th minute they opted for tighter marking distances to transition more promptly into full man-marking. Brown pushed up directly, Theate went straight onto Sané, while Collins and Koch marked the two remaining forwards. This created a 3v3 situation on the last line. Although this increased the pressure on Galatasaray and led to more turnovers in their build-up, it also raised the risk against long balls due to isolated 1v1s. Time and again, Galatasaray managed to exploit this by sending strong dribblers like Sané into such spacious 1v1 situations. Even so, the tighter marking distances resulted in a much more balanced game with more frequent ball recoveries.

    Recent findings suggest that in the 30th minute, Frankfurt used a longer stoppage to make more significant pressing adjustments. Winger Knauff no longer pressed Galatasaray’s right centre-back but instead oriented himself toward full-back Sallai. This allowed Brown to stay on Sané, and Theate no longer had to make long runs out wide to cover him. At the same time, it was no longer problematic if all four defenders were tied up, as they no longer needed to jump out of the back line. The free centre-back was now primarily pressed by Uzun, who used his cover shadow to block passing lanes into pivot Torreira. Galatasaray’s build-up on the right side could then be pressed man-to-man through ball-oriented shifting. To this end, Chaibi stepped onto Uzun’s original opponent, Torreira, and the far-side Doan also moved into the ball-near center.

    Recent findings suggest that frankfurt’s pressing adjustments: With no need to shift across the last line anymore, Frankfurt gains situationally much better access with less risk. These changes spark the turnaround in the match.

    The pressing adjustments led to significantly better situational access and, at the same time, to much stronger defensive security. Frankfurt were able to use the resulting ball recoveries to establish longer possession phases, which gave them a more dominant style of play. One such spell of possession resulted in the 2-1 lead shortly before halftime. Immediately afterwards, a ball recovery from the adjusted attacking press led to a free kick, which in turn produced the 3-1 at the break.

    In the opening 30 minutes, Galatasaray were able to cause Frankfurt problems, thanks in part to a very elusive build-up play that challenged Frankfurt’s typical pressing approach with its reliance on handover moments. Frankfurt’s adjustments, however, proved perfectly suited to applying pressure more easily while also improving defensive cover. The short interruption of play came at just the right time for Toppmöller and his coaching staff to implement the necessary measures. As a result, the pressing changes were decisive for Frankfurt’s eventual 5-1 victory and a successful start to their Champions League campaign.

    #3726. Ranking the NBA's most hopeless teams: Which franchise is in the bleakest situation? And who can't fix it?

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 11m • 📚 Deep Dive (2142 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    Ranking the NBA's most hopeless teams: Which franchise is in the bleakest situation? And who can't fix it?

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2142 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, the Milwaukee Bucks faced Giannis Antetokounmpo as an opponent for the first time on Wednesday, and it didn't go well.
    • Milwaukee knew it would spend this season in the cellar.
    • Industry observers note that to be clear here, we are operating in terms of championship equity.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, the Milwaukee Bucks faced Giannis Antetokounmpo as an opponent for the first time on Wednesday, and it didn't go well. Though the final score showed only a seven-point margin, the Miami Heat led by 26 after three quarters and were never in much danger. The defeat dropped the Bucks to 1-14 on the season. The greatest player in their franchise's history now wears another jersey, and they're at the beginning of what figures to be a very long rebuild. Things are bleak.

    The question here is how bleak. Milwaukee knew it would spend this season in the cellar. It probably expects to live there for a few years. But how far away from winning seriously are the Bucks really? Are they further from genuine contention than any other team in the NBA? Who, right now, has the bleakest long-term outlook?

    Industry observers note that to be clear here, we are operating in terms of championship equity. We don't care if you have a chance to be a plucky .500 team. No, the barometer we're using here is how likely each team is to reach a conference finals in the next five seasons. We're accounting not only for players on the existing roster, but long-term financial flexibility, available draft assets and the competence of the front office helming these organizations. With all of that in mind, let's rank the NBA's most hopeless long-term outlooks.

    Industry observers note that the broad sentiment following their punishment for circumventing the salary cap with Kawhi Leonard was that the Clippers faced the bleakest future in the entire NBA. That's probably overstating things slightly.

    Remember, we're talking about a Los Angeles team here. Someone, inevitably, is going to want to play for them. All it takes is one player bucking the league-wide trend against superstar free agency and they're back in business. They have an owner who will spare no expense in pursuit of wins, and there's a 26-year-old All-Star in Darius Garland already on the roster. Couple that with the hope generated by No. 5 overall pick Keaton Wagler, and while the path here is extremely narrow, it exists. If the Brooklyn Nets could build a contender without draft picks in the late 2010s, it's theoretically possible for the Clippers to do the same.

    Of course, the Nets weren't subject to that league-wide pivot away from free agency. They didn't have to trade picks to get Kevin Durant or Kyrie Irving in the door. It's much, much harder nowadays to import talent like that without sacrificing picks that the Clippers frankly don't have. The five first-round picks they were docked in the Leonard investigation left them fully Stepien-locked: while they will have (not especially valuable) first-round picks in odd-numbered years moving forward, they can't trade any of them yet.

    There's also the reputational hit the Clippers just took. Will players interested in winning want to risk their careers on a team that cheated? Can the Clippers even appeal to such players given their asset deficit? These are going to be real hurdles. Their path to the conference finals might rely on a star who's not especially competitive. After all, anyone serious about winning could find a team closer to doing so.

    Sources indicate that they're a blank slate with one very promising prospect. Darius Acuff is putting up star box-score numbers in his rookie season. That's by no means a guarantee of future stardom, of course. He's as inefficient as you'd expect a rookie to be on this volume. He's taking more shots per game than Jalen Brunson, Tyrese Maxey or Dwyane Wade ever did over a full season. But Acuff has a path to becoming one of the NBA's best offensive point guards. These aren't totally empty calories.

    There's nothing else here. No other notable prospects aside from a handful of likely long-term bench youngsters (Dylan Cardwell, Maxime Raynaud, Emanuel Sharp). Sacramento mostly controls its own picks (aside from the 2031 swap it inexplicably gave San Antonio in the DeMar DeRozan sign-and-trade), but that means less than it used to in the lottery reform era. Its books slowly clean up in the offseasons to come, with Zach LaVine and De'Andre Hunter expiring after this season and Domantas Sabonis and Malik Monk joining them in the summer of 2028, but Sacramento's forays into cap space have typically been unsuccessful. This isn't exactly a desirable destination. That's what happens when you miss the playoffs 19 times in 20 years.

    It has been revealed that that's what separates Sacramento from fellow "one possible star, otherwise blank slate" candidates like the Chicago Bulls. With the hire of Bryson Graham to run basketball operations, the Bulls at least appear to be trending towards becoming a normal organization. Normalcy has eternally eluded Sacramento. The burden of proof is on the Kings. When you've been a mess for 20 years, it's on you to prove that you've cleaned up your act. We'll trust the Kings when they've earned it and not a second sooner.

    For now, they can at least start by actually keeping their success stories in the building. They've kept only one first-round pick this decade through the end of his rookie contract: Keegan Murray, who is now pretty substantially overpaid. Meanwhile, Tyrese Haliburton has blossomed into a superstar in Indiana, while their entire 2021 draft class (Davion Mitchell and Neemias Queta) now starts for Eastern Conference championship hopefuls. They had the unanimous Coach of the Year and the Executive of the Year and fired both within two years. The Kings can't help themselves.

    It has been revealed that there's far more talent in the cupboard here than in Sacramento, but the same organizational concerns apply. The Joe Dumars regime makes mistakes -- the two-year minimum for DeAndre Jordan, not waiting until after the 2025 Finals to trade Indiana its 2026 pick back, everything Shamit Dua has reported about the infamous Derik Queen trade -- that typical teams would never dream of.

    According to recent reports, there is not a discernible plan here besides, seemingly, "acquire players who can put the ball through the hoop." There are a lot of decent individual creators on this roster. None of them synergize well because so few of them can consistently make 3s and all of them are on-ball players with stylistic clashes. The Pelicans have seemingly made the determination, for instance, that Queen cannot play significant minutes alongside Zion Williamson. That's a reasonable choice... but then why is Williamson still on the team? Or, if the Pelicans view him as a fixture, why make such a risky trade for Queen in the first place?

    According to recent reports, the trickle-down effect of putting all of these dribblers on the same team is that none of them seem happy to be on it. Dejounte Murray asked for a trade. Jordan Poole is making googly eyes at the Warriors. Trey Murphy has reportedly signaled a desire to move. What is the strategy here? What kind of team are the Pelicans trying to build? What do they view as their path to genuine winning?

    According to recent reports, that's what distinguishes New Orleans from Sacramento. If the Kings get a few more high draft picks and use them on players that complement Acuff, I'd see the vision. It would require Acuff becoming an All-NBA scorer and those picks hitting, but I see the sort of teams they could build, even if they're unlikely to actually do so. I have no earthly idea what the Pelicans would do with a few high picks because talent is not right now the problem. It's how they're using and nurturing it. It's just hard to envision a team with so little understanding of how to balance skill sets and bring out the best in their players making a serious playoff push. Something significant in the organization would have to change.

    Recent findings suggest that they're the best team on this list in the present, and they've clawed their way back to .500 after a miserable start that included leaks about the team's lack of a point guard. Again, we're dealing in upside here. That's what the Suns lack.

    Industry observers note that they control none of their own first-round picks in the seven-year tradable window except for their 2032 selection... which is frozen because they spent the 2024-25 season above the second apron. Even if they had picks, the Suns under Matt Ishbia have never displayed any discipline in using them. Ishbia traded nearly a full draft for Kevin Durant mere days after acquiring the team, spent an unprotected 2031 pick on three far lesser choices that amounted to Mark Williams and a Jusuf Nurkić cap dump, and then spent their 2033 pick as soon as they could access it to get Miles Bridges, whom they've been meaningfully better without thus far this season.

    It has been revealed that the most talented players here are all right around their physical peaks. Devin Booker is 30. Dillon Brooks turns 31 this season, and Bridges turns 29. They're going to get worse, not better, and without draft picks, their means of replacing them are minimal. Even the diamonds they've dug out of the rough are on the older side. Collin Gillespie is 27. Jordan Goodwin is 28. The truly young players, like Khaman Maluach and Rasheer Fleming, have thus far underwhelmed. The younger, star-level talent here is Jalen Green, who plays Booker's position and has been a disaster on both ends this season. Why exactly is he still starting over Gillespie? Are the Suns just trying to salvage his trade value?

    Teams like the Clippers, Kings and Pelicans are at least young enough and financially flexible enough to grow. The Suns, at least from an asset and financial standpoint, are essentially all-in on a Play-In-caliber roster. That Play-In-caliber roster is going to get worse as it gets older and more expensive and, without access to top talent in the draft, replenishing it is going to be borderline impossible.

    The Bucks cherry-pick traits from all of our other selections. The Clippers circumvented the cap; the Bucks are getting investigated for doing so with Gary Trent Jr. The Pelicans have a roster full of overlapping skill sets; the Bucks have a million shooting guards, which made the decision to re-sign Trent for $64 million all the stranger. The Suns don't control any of their own picks and the Bucks won't until 2031 at the earliest. The Kings have the NBA's least-successful owner in Vivek Ranadivé, while the Bucks may have the NFL's in Jimmy Haslam, though he technically won't become governor until 2028 due to Milwaukee's bizarre ownership structure (another point against them, as successful teams tend to have stable leadership rather than rotating five-year terms).

    Who is going to be the best player on the team in five years? Brayden Burries is the best long-term prospect, but he profiles as more of a high-end role player. Tyler Herro was an All-Star in the sense that Norman Powell and D'Angelo Russell were All-Stars: they put up major numbers in a weak Eastern Conference. Kel'El Ware was the lottery ticket from the Giannis Antetokounmpo trade and he's been so bad that he's somehow playing less than he did on a Heat team that was trying to win. Without access to their own picks or a market that tends to draw free agents, they're basically hoping someone internal (Nate Ament? Ryan Rollins?) breaks out or that they hit on a pick far later than you should rely on.

    You could argue that just by virtue of being in the Eastern Conference, the Bucks have a cleaner path to the final four than those West teams do because they don't have to worry about Victor Wembanyama or the specter of healthier versions of the Oklahoma City Thunder down the line. That's fair, but as we've seen this year, injuries loom over every season. You know what else the West has aside from those two juggernauts? The four other teams on this list. The Bucks, by a wide margin, are the most hopeless team in their own conference. They're starting from the absolute bottom.

    This was potentially avoidable. Had they acted sooner and traded Antetokounmpo in 2025 when the whole world knew a deal was eventually coming, they could have secured a stronger return and set themselves up for a quicker turnaround. Alas, the Bucks chose to waive-and-stretch Damian Lillard, locking them into $22.5 million in dead money through the end of the decade so they could sign Myles Turner to a contract that is increasingly looking like $28 million or so per year in... close to dead money. Milwaukee got its championship in 2021, but at this rate, it's going to be a while before it sniffs another one.

    #3724. Luis Castillo trade grades: White Sox give up steady back-end starter to offload salary; Rockies get creative

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (663 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    Luis Castillo trade grades: White Sox give up steady back-end starter to offload salary; Rockies get creative

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (663 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that two days after adding Dustin May to their rotation, the Chicago White Sox have subtracted Luis Castillo and Davis Martin.
    • Castillo, 33, joined the White Sox in a deadline trade with the Seattle Mariners.
    • The 29-year-old Martin threw 146 innings with a 3.95 ERA in 2026, but it was a 3.41 ERA in the first half and a 5.12 ERA in the second half.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that two days after adding Dustin May to their rotation, the Chicago White Sox have subtracted Luis Castillo and Davis Martin. The White Sox are sending Castillo and Martin to the Colorado Rockies for lefty Sean Sullivan and minor-league catcher Douglas Veliz, the teams announced late Thursday. The Rockies will take on Castillo's entire contract.

    Castillo, 33, joined the White Sox in a deadline trade with the Seattle Mariners. He struggled badly after the deal, allowing 30 runs in 31 innings, and he finished the season on the injured list with a shoulder problem. Castillo has one year remaining on his contract at $22.75 million, though a $25 million option for 2028 will vest if he throws 150 innings in 2027.

    The 29-year-old Martin threw 146 innings with a 3.95 ERA in 2026, but it was a 3.41 ERA in the first half and a 5.12 ERA in the second half. The White Sox kept him at arm's length in the postseason despite running bullpen games almost nightly. Martin allowed two runs in one inning in his only postseason appearance.

    In a recent development, neither Sullivan nor Veliz are significant prospects. For all intents and purposes, the White Sox are attaching Martin to Castillo as a sweetener to get the Rockies to take Castillo's salary. The Rockies are essentially buying Martin, who is under team control through 2030, by taking on the rest of Castillo's contract.

    Here now are our trade grades for this two-for-two swap.

    Fair or not, I'm going to lump the two Castillo trades together. Chicago stepped out to acquire Castillo at the deadline and absorbed the $30 million or so remaining on his contract to do it. Seranthony Domínguez, who had about $15 million left on his deal, went the other way in the trade, so the White Sox took on about $15 million total, and also gave up a pretty good prospect in Boston Smith.

    Four and a half months later, the White Sox had to give up a steady back-end starter in Martin to clear Castillo's money. They ended up saving about $7 million in 2027 in this series of moves, but it cost them Martin and Smith (and Domínguez), and they had to endure 31 awful innings from Castillo. Unless Sullivan or Veliz hit substantial, the White Sox took a series of Ls here.

    Credit to president of baseball operations Chris Getz for acknowledging a mistake with Castillo and acting swiftly to unload him. It was costly, though. Martin isn't a star, but cheap back-end starters are very valuable. We'll see what Getz & Co. do with the savings. Presumably they'll invest in more pitching. Having to give up Martin to dump Castillo so soon is a stinker, though. Ouch.

    The Rockies need all types of pitching (righty, lefty, starter, reliever, whatever) and it's not often they can convince quality (or even competent) free agents to come to Coors Field. They have to develop their own pitchers or trade for pitching, and in this instance, they took on Castillo's hefty salary to get Martin and his four years of control. Creative, if nothing else.

    There is downside potential too. Martin has run below league-average strikeout rates and middling ground ball rates throughout his career. Pitchers who allow a lot of balls in play -- a lot of balls in play in the air -- are a poor match for Coors Field. It's good the Rockies spent and found a way to add controllable pitching. They just might not have picked the best pitcher.

    After losing 104 games in 2026, there is no such thing as a bad dart throw for the Rockies. It's unlikely they would have been able to spend the $22.75 million on a free agent (at least not without overpaying), so taking on Castillo to get Martin is the next best thing. I like the thinking, even if I don't love Martin's profile in Coors Field.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Brooklyn Nets are no strangers to losing games this season, as they fell to 3-11 on Wednesday night, but in a season filled with lopsided defeats, losing by 30 points to the Chicago Bulls stood out as a upcoming low point.

    Recent findings suggest that the Bulls also entered Wednesday's game at 3-10 on the season, operating as one of the league's worst teams so far, but Chicago exploded for 137 points against the Nets, with eight players reaching double figures. While Chicago's biggest issue has come on the defensive end this season, the Bulls haven't exactly been lighting opponents up offensively, sitting 23rd in the league in offensive rating.

    The Nets' complete inability to put up a resistance against the Bulls rang alarm bells in Brooklyn and had veteran Julius Randle calling out his team for an "embarrassing" and "unacceptable" performance.

    "I've been in the league for 13 years... that's one of the worst games I've ever been a part of."Julius Randle didn't hold back after the Nets’ 30-point loss to Bulls. 😳 pic.twitter.com/s3YQ8TxP35.

    "The main struggle? I don't know, that was embarrassing," Randle stated after the game. "Been in the league for 13 years and that's one of the worst games I've ever been a part of. And not because of the score. You lose by 30 sometimes -- it's just a bad night -- but it's how we did it. That just, it wasn't cool. Nothing about it was cool. We gotta find a way to figure out the root of it or whatever, but that just is unacceptable.".

    Considering Randle has been on his fair share of bad basketball teams over his career in Los Angeles, New Orleans and New York, that's saying something.

    There are five teams that have separated themselves from the pack at the bottom of the NBA in terms of defense and the Nets are one of them with a 119.0 defensive rating (26th in the league). No one expected much of Brooklyn on that end of the floor with the roster they've assembled, but it's one thing to have lesser talent on the defensive end; it's another to combine that with a general lack of effort.

    According to recent reports, this early in the season, the latter is a much larger concern and the Nets have now given up at least 124 points in five of their last six games. If they were able to shrug off some of those lopsided losses to quality teams as life in the NBA, Wednesday was proof that their problems extend far beyond just some schedule losses.

    Giving up 137 to a Bulls team that's been similarly bad this year is, in Randle's words, unacceptable. The concern is that no one in Brooklyn, including Randle, seems quite sure what the exact problem is or how to fix it.
