    #3660. Arsenal hunger is ominous for rivals as they dismantle Man City

    📅 16 Aug 2026 • ⏱️ 30m • 📚 Deep Dive (5934 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

    Arsenal hunger is ominous for rivals as they dismantle Man City

    📅 16 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 30 min read (5934 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~30 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Was it the early goal that should have put Arsenal’s rivals on red alert?
    • In a recent development, how about the emphatic scoreline – surely that was it?
    • Recent findings suggest that so what was it that should have those with pretensions of ripping Arsenal’s crown from their grasp shuffling uncomfortably?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Was it the early goal that should have put Arsenal’s rivals on red alert? No. While Ricardo Calafiori’s intervention was dramatic, it wasn’t that. Was it the seamless introduction of the latest signings, then? No, it wasn’t that either, despite the excellence of Bruno Guimarães and Christos Tzolis.

    In a recent development, how about the emphatic scoreline – surely that was it? Again, the answer is no. Three unanswered goals against Manchester City will always grab a headline, but scorelines do not always define the nature of a performance or a team’s capabilities.

    Recent findings suggest that so what was it that should have those with pretensions of ripping Arsenal’s crown from their grasp shuffling uncomfortably? One word: hunger. The reason this was such an ominous afternoon for the chasing pack is the fact Mikel Arteta’s team played with intensity of a team with everything to prove.

    Title wins can sometimes sate ambition. Players don’t always want to climb the same mountain again, not least if reaching the peak was initially so draining, but everywhere you looked on a day when Cardiff was painted red and white was evidence that Arsenal remain ravenous for success.

    First Guimarães pounced out of the shadows to mug Jérémy Doku, leaving him in a heap. Then there was Gabriel Magalhães thundering into a befuddled Doku, celebrating in front of City’s fans as if he had scored, before Ben White flung himself in front of the Belgian, denying a clear-cut scoring opportunity.

    Ben White to the rescue with an incredible block 🦸📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ZK0cNnFz5N.

    It has been revealed that another notable incident was Martin Odegaard, not long after he had glossed a fabulous display with a third goal, sprinting 30 yards to spook Gianluigi Donnarumma and make the Italian hurry his clearance. The victory was good, the trophy was nice, but the energy heartened Arteta more than anything.

    In a recent development, “They are really good examples,” Arteta said. “The way the team tracks back is unbelievable, especially when, fitness-wise, we aren’t there yet. We had desire and composure on the ball. When you put your soul and your heart into every action, this is what happens. We want to do it again.

    “The desire comes from them thinking: ‘I want to live that moment again. I want to have all the moments again and I want them to be even bigger.’ We know what it is going to take. We have never done it [retain the Premier League] at this football club. We know it will demand something special.”.

    Industry observers note that you could flip that and say it will take something special from the chasers. George Graham and Arsène Wenger could never hold on to the biggest prize during their reigns and you must return to Herbert Chapman, in Arsenal’s thriving 1930s, to find the only manager who went back-to-back.

    It can feel premature (and can be foolish) to go out on a limb before the first weekend, but there was just something about them that felt different. Often in the past they have been overtly tentative when playing City, but they came out of their corner this time swinging – and they landed.

    Enzo Maresca revealed afterwards that he “really didn’t like” how Arsenal had scored their first goal and that was putting it mildly, as there were 10 passes – broken only by the ball bouncing off Elliott Anderson’s shins – before Myles Lewis-Skelly ushered Calafiori into wreak havoc.

    You had to go back to 1968, when City played West Brom, to find the last first-minute goal – City’s Bobby Owen was the scorer that day – and how Calafiori enjoyed it, shaking his fist in delight as Arsenal’s noisy fans reminded everyone of their status.

    Riccardo Calafiori gives Arsenal the lead after just 24 seconds 🤯The assist from Myles Lewis-Skelly 👏📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/aU0UsCB1Xs.

    Here was a rude awakening for Anderson, City’s newly introduced £116m man. He was ever so slightly off the pace and that allowed Lewis-Skelly to slip a beautiful ball in behind the FA Cup winners’ defence and invite Calafiori to do the rest, which he did with assurance.

    When Maresca watches back the video, he will see Abdukodir Khusanov sleeping and Phil Foden failing to press, but that should not detract from the quality of Arsenal’s interchanging – and it should also make whoever is hawking Lewis-Skelly around to clubs to think again. Why would he leave this?

    Recent findings suggest that it should not have been the case that a goal so soon should have governed how the game progressed, but that is exactly what happened as Arsenal completely dominated. Whenever they lost possession, they recovered it as a matter of urgency. Without Pep Guardiola on the touchline, City were like Samson after Delilah shaved his hair, devoid of all power.

    Recent findings suggest that city, in contrast to their opponents, showed a complete lack of desire and the second goal arrived when Odegaard was allowed time to flip a ball to the back post, where new boy Tzolis was arriving. The Greek headed back into the six-yard area and Kai Havertz did the rest.

    Kai Havertz finishes off a well-worked move to double Arsenal's lead 🤩📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/tGkxCIBV8F.

    Arsenal were criticised – fairly – during their title-winning campaign for being too physical and relying on gamesmanship, but if Havertz and Odegaard can stay fit for a prolonged period, the difference in style will be like night and day.

    Throw in Tzolis, who was tricky and dynamic in Cardiff, to the mix and there will be another enhancement. He looks considerably better than Gabriel Martinelli, with more end product, and Bukayo Saka will do more down the right than Noni Madueke, who started here.

    Maresca knew, with his team lacking fitness, that it would be difficult to overhaul the deficit once they had gone two goals behind but, really, he was lucky that Arsenal did not administer a genuine hiding which, at one stage, seemed as though they might.

    Goal number three arrived just after the interval, again Lewis-Skelly and Tzolis were involved, combining to enable Odegaard to waltz into the area, hoodwinking Donnarumma so he sat down before sliding a contemptuous finish beyond him.

    Take a bow, Martin Ødegaard 😮‍💨Arsenal are flying against Man City!📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/cMHbIyJ90D.

    Had they gone through the gears, there could have been more, but it didn’t matter. What Arsenal highlighted was far more significant than a couple of more goals when the game was being disrupted by substitutions. The tackles, the running, energy and commitment – that is what brought Arteta joy.

    “I’m extremely happy with the performance, the result and winning the first trophy,” Arteta purred.

    You would be brave to say it will be their last.

    Arsenal (4-2-3-1) Raya 7; White 7, Mosquera 7, Gabriel 7, Calafiori 7 (Hincapie h-t): Guimarães 7 (Rice h-t), Lewis-Skelly 8 (Zublimendi 75); Madueke 6 [Saka 60], Odegaard 8 (Eze 84), Tzolis 7; Havertz 7 (Gyokeres 75). Booked Calafiori, Odegaard. Subs Kepa (g), Merino, Dowman.

    Goals: Calafiori (1), Havertz (28), Odegaard (48).

    Manchester City (4-2-3-1) Donnarumma 5; Khusnaov 5, Dias 5, Gvardiol 5, O’Reilly 5; Anderson 5 (Lewis 60), Kovacic 5 (Gonzalez 79); Semenyo 6, Foden 5 (Cherki 60), Doku 6 (Grealish h-t); Haaland 5 (Marmoush 53). Booked Gvardiol, Foden. Subs Ait-Nouri, Reis, Nunes, Rulli (g).

    Referee Sam Barrott (Yorkshire).

    Industry observers note that it’s really sad. I’ve been fighting with the Premier League to extend & accommodate more players in the squad. They deserve to be in the squad, so hopefully we can change that rule.

    I think the goal we conceded after 25 seconds unfortunately affected the game in that moment. I think after the goal, the reaction was quite good before they scored the second one, we had three or four chances to score and draw the game but unfortunately we conceded the second one and it became more complicated.

    A really, really good performance so early in the season. To play at the level we did and the desire we showed, I just told them that I really enjoyed watching them.

    He makes good decisions when a lot of people rush things, he did it twice in tight areas and two goals.

    I joined midway [in pre-season]. This is the third game since I have been back. The feeling has been good. Today is frustrating, and it is a final that we all wanted to win. If there is a lesson to be learnt in the final, let it be this one, as there’s a lot more coming. It is a positive energy.

    The feeling of a lot of work to put into. It’s part of any transition for things to be not so perfect in the beginning. You need to push through, you need to communicate, and make things work between us. I feel we’re in a very good way, but we need to keep on working. There’s going to be lots of challenges along the way.

    Appears to the Community Shield trophy, which caught him a glancing blow to the face.

    Trophy lift gone wrong, featuring Declan Rice 😂🏆📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ghmGZJDxka.

    Sources indicate that the players judge the correct level of celebration judiciously, but then Mikel Merino cracks and starts spraying the champagne. While it is a semi-competitive game, Arteta and his players will point out that they earned their place in the fixture by winning the league.

    Arsenal start the season with silverware 🏆The Community Shield belongs to the Gunners!📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/M6GqsGkRF7.

    What happens to them? I’m not sure the winners’ medals would take pride of place, let alone the silvers.

    We played some brilliant football. Great performance and a great way to start the season.

    I always want to help the team as much possible with goals and assists. I want to score more goals.

    It has been revealed that we indicated our level today. We’re showed we’re ready. We’re serious and we want to do it again.

    Recent findings suggest that we want to attack it. We want to do it again. When you get a taste of how nice it is you want to do it again.

    Recent findings suggest that the league champions kick-off the domestic season with a resounding and stylish victory. Shades of 1998 and 2004 when they swept Manchester United aside in this fixture as title winners, only to fail to defend the crown in the season that followed. So maybe it is unwise to make bold forecasts, but it could not have gone better for Arteta. Odegaard, Lewis-Skelly and Tzolis caught the eye, and Arsenal had their usual solidarity defensively. City just completely off the pace, one to write off and move on.

    Marmoush is feeling his hip after a challenge by Mosquera. City have a free-kick wide right. Gabriel heads away Grealish’s delivery in trademark fashion.

    Just three minutes of added time to play. No City player is there to meet Cherki’s low cross and White can clear under little pressure.

    Rice uncharacteristically caught dallying in midfield but City cannot capitalise. Cheers from the Arsenal fans as Saka wins a throw in from Grealish. Marmoush with a chance to run at Mosquera, but his touch is far too heavy.

    City have a free-kick in a crossing position right of centre, but many of their fans are now packing up their banners and heading for the exits. If they haven’t already. Cherki’s delivery is poor, and Rice heads away.

    Odegaard with a loose touch, and a yellow card for catching Grealish with the resulting challenge. That was the Arsenal captain’s last action of the game, he is replaced by Eberechi Eze. Odegaard has looked back to his 2024 past today, Eze’s best chance of a start might be from the left.

    City’s best move of the second half: Cherki gliding through the challenges and finding Semenyo with a lovely reverse pass, and his shot was drilled towards the far corner. Sharp reflexes by Raya to plunge to his right and save.

    Sources indicate that nico Gonzalez replaces Kovacic as Maresca makes his sixth change of the second half. The game has felt like a training exercise since Odegaard’s third goal with the occasional flash of quality.

    Industry observers note that chance for Saka! Cracking low cross from Hincapie, but Saka sweeps over from near the penalty spot. Too much on it as he tried to help the ball on its way.

    Better tempo to Manchester City’s football, and Gvardiol has gone down holding his face in the box. It was more of a shoulder to shoulder with White, and the incident is checked and cleared by VAR.

    Here come two more Arsenal changes: Havertz and Lewis-Skelly deserve their ovation, replaced by Gyokeres and Zubimendi.

    According to recent reports, chance for Tzolis to play Saka clean through on goal but he delayed a fraction and Gvardiol got back in to defend. It was a great flick on by Havertz to free Tzolis. Gyokeres is ready to replace the German.

    Cherki with a shot from distance, saved by Raya. That was City’s first shot on target of the second half.

    In a recent development, odegaard with a disguised ball through to White, who may have been offside, and Tzolis is close to applying the touch that would have made it four. Feels like the game is meandering towards its conclusion.

    Arsenal back themselves to play out from a tight spot again, but Semenyo does well to force Hincapie to concede a throw in. Arsenal then soak up another spell of City possession, they have been so much more compact defensively than Maresca’s team. Whenever Arsenal have the ball in City’s half they look dangerous, whereas City’s possession has been sterile.

    Industry observers note that city chasing shadows when Arsenal play out from the back. Arsenal moving the ball with great assurance, but you suspect everyone has an extra yard of space than they would find in a full-throttle Premier League game.

    Semenyo gave Hincapie a tough time in the League Cup final in March, and was not shy in boasting about it after the game. I suspect Hincapie is a defender who keeps a little black book of those who have crossed him.

    Lovely moment in midfield from Odegaard, letting the ball run across his box and pushing it beyond Rico Lewis. Saka in acres on the far side after he outmuscles Gvardiol, but he shoots into the side netting. Tried to give Donnarumma the eyes.

    City with a spell of possession in the Arsenal half, and Gvardiol glances a header over the bar from a very decent Grealish cross. Arsenal hard to break down once they are in that 4-4-2 shape.

    Here come the changes: Foden and Anderson off, Cherki and Rico Lewis on.

    Industry observers note that arsenal subs: Saka and Hincapue on for Calafiori and Madueke. Saka has braids this seasons, so a newly introduced look.

    Arsenal popping the ball around in the sunshine now, to olés from their fans. Maresca is about to make two more changes, so five subs before the hour tells you were City are physically. Saka is going to come on for Arsenal.

    In a recent development, gvardiol booked, and here come more City changes, this is a fitness exercise for Maresca now. Haaland and O’Reilly off, Marmoush and Guehi on. Arteta will surely reply in kind around the hour mark.

    That really should be game over now, but given the loosey-goosey nature of these games I suppose you never know. I think the only way this fixture can matter is if one team takes a battering, and there’s a risk of that for City now.

    It has been revealed that christos Tzolis registered 29 assists in 52 competitive games for Club Brugge last season. He’s on two assists in 48 competitive minutes for Arsenal.

    What composure from the Arsenal captain, running into the box untracked and sitting down first Gvardiol then Donnarumma before finding the empty net. It is clever play from Tzolis, finding Odegaard with the pass for his second assist of the game. The run from Calafiori was crucial to pull City’s defence out of shape.

    Take a bow, Martin Ødegaard 😮‍💨Arsenal are flying against Man City!📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/cMHbIyJ90D.

    Sources indicate that man City kick off in the second 45 minutes. These matches tend to lose their rhythm in the second half.

    So far, Manchester City’s first glimpse of life after Pep Guardiola is inauspicious. Enzo Maresca might be his predecessor’s doppelgänger, but his attempt to emulate the same style has proved abortive: plenty of possession, but minimal impact. It smacks of desperation that Jack Grealish is being thrown in at half-time, his first appearance for the club for 15 months.

    Looks like a pre-planned change from Manchester City and Arsenal: Jack Grealish makes an unlikely comeback, replacing Doku, and Declan Rice replaces Bruno Guimaraes. Arsenal’s two significant hitters in midfield sharing the game.

    Sources indicate that 7 - Kai Havertz has been involved in more goals against Manchester City (7 - 4 goals, 3 assists) than against any other side in his club career. Occasion. pic.twitter.com/ln7PQnjboJ.

    It has been revealed that 00:23 - Riccardo Calafiori's goal for Arsenal after 23 seconds is the first scored in the opening minute of the Community Shield since Bobby Owen for Manchester City against West Bromwich Albion in 1968.Rapid. pic.twitter.com/FCwVKuTOlh.

    Advantage Arsenal at half time, and they have looked a sharper, more cohesive team. City have had plenty of possession, but much of it was sterile until that late flurry when Raya saved from Haaland and White blocked Doku’s shot. The first 45 minutes will have ticked all of the boxes for Arteta: there has been some strong penalty box defending, some flowing moves from back to front and two well-taken goals.

    Flimsy defending from City again, Havertz finding it easy to run to the byline, and the ball is cleared off the line after Odegaard poked the ball towards goal after a Donnarumma parry.

    “You’re getting sacked in the morning,” sing the Arsenal fans at Maresca as the whistle blows.

    Mosquera defends well against Doku at the expense of a corner, which Raya claims with ease. There is going to be just one minute of added time.

    Arsenal playing through the pitch and City’s defensive shape again, this time it was started by a fizzed Raya pass into Tzolis. Three on three, but Madueke’s shot is straight at Donnarummma. The winger is such an outlet for his team, but the final decision is lacking too often, which is not a novel observation.

    Madueke then finds White on the overlap, he chips the ball to the back post where Calafiori is free and he volleys over.

    Arsenal’s defence stretched for the first time in the game. Raya saved after Haaland was picked out by Doku, with Lewis-Skelly defending well to deny a rebound, before Semenyo picks out Doku with a lofted cross, but White through himself in front of the volley and made a crucial block.

    Ben White to the rescue with an incredible block 🦸📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ZK0cNnFz5N.

    Madueke with a tame shot on goal after O’Reilly went Awol defensively, but the flag was up for offside.

    Arsenal come forward again, with Havertz holding the ball up well. Tzolis reverses a pass for Calafiori, but he anticipates a challenge in the area and is rightly booked for diving.

    Ben White thought he had nipped in front of Doku to intercept a straight Kovacic pass, but the referee blows for a foul against the Arsenal man.

    In a recent development, then Haaland has a sight of goal for the first time: a peeling run into the right channel, found by Doku, but it was tough angle on his weaker foot. Scooped it over the bar.

    Sources indicate that foden takes up a lovely position behind the Arsenal midfield, but his through ball towards Haaland hits Gabriel on the back of the heel. Then Semenyo wins a corner in a joust with Calafiori. Referee blows for some pushing and shoving.

    Eventually the corner is taken, cleared initially, before teasing Foden cross drifts beyond the back post. Foden the pick of the bunch for City, which is unsurprising considering he has a full pre-season behind him.

    It has been revealed that the Arsenal supporters are really, really enjoying this. They’re “doing the Poznan” to mock the City fans.

    An ideal outing for Arsenal, so far though it can be easy to over-index these games when players are not fully match fit. But Arteta will be pleased with the fluency in the passing through midfield, which was lacking at times last season.

    Christos Tzolis was signed to provide goals and assists, and he’s been doing so throughout pre-season. The Greek winger is perhaps more aggressive in his positioning than Leandro Trossard, the man he has replaced in the squad, and he was in the right place there to pick out Kai Havertz.

    Sources indicate that the new signing Tzolis is involved with a clever header back across the six-yard box, the left winger was picked out by an inswinging Odegaard cross to the back post. Havertz rose above Dias, and his header down into the turf squeezed beyond Donnarumma. The ball bounced in off the back of the goalkeeper, could well be an own goal.

    Kai Havertz finishes off a well-worked move to double Arsenal's lead 🤩📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/tGkxCIBV8F.

    Gvardiol slides across to win an notable challenge when Madueke was running into space, before Odegaard fails with a scooped pass towards White.

    Recent findings suggest that arsenal find Madueke in acres of space again, Bruno Guimaraes with the switch, and the winger keeps things alive despite an unconvincing dribble. Guimaraes then finds space in the box, but takes to long to pick out a man.

    In a recent development, city soon on the attack again, and Doku runs off the back of White all too easily, but Gabriel charges in to win a booming slide tackle in the box. He greets it with his own roar of approval.

    Raya claims the corner, then Foden is booked for pulling back Tzolis to stop a counter.

    In these early days, long before trophies become something tangible, Mikel Arteta will want to see something far more vital than talent - hunger. It’s bursting out of Arsenal’s players, never more apparent than when Gabriel has just thundered into Jeremy Doku and celebrated the challenge like a goal. It reflective of the team’s mentality.

    The passion from Gabriel after stopping Jérémy Doku 😤📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/L3D8lHrBNU.

    Sources indicate that city’s best moment so far: Foden with a shot from just outside the box which is pushed clear by Raya, before O’Reilly is penalised for a push on Ben White. It looked like the City man was just stronger in the shoulder to shoulder. Perhaps out frustration, O’Reilly then fouls Havertz on halfway.

    The Arsenal fans massively outnumber the City supporters here, and the Londoners appear to have fallen in love with Guimaraes already. He’s snapping into tackles with real venom. There have been lots of cries of “Bruno!” in these opening 23 minutes.

    Recent findings suggest that better from City, with Foden turning after receiving the ball between the lines. Then Anderson flashes a cross across the penalty area from an inside right position, but Haaland was slightly on his heels and it runs out for a goal kick.

    Interesting to see Guimaraes drop all the way into Arsenal’s penalty area for their goal-kick a few minutes ago. Arsenal had massive problems playing out from the back against City in the Carabao Cup final last season. The Brazilian’s positioning could be a reaction to that.

    In a recent development, considering Arsenal are missing Saliba, Timber and Rice, their defence has looked relatively untroubled so far. City’s big names in attacking areas are on the pitch, but still finding their level as the newly introduced season approaches.

    According to recent reports, arsenal have a corner after Gvardiol sticks out a leg to block Madueke’s low cross. Sharp in midfield from Lewis-Skelly and Bruno Guimaraes to spread the play to the right winger. Good delivery from Madueke, headed clear, before White does well to usher the ball behind for another corner.

    Gabriel and Khusanov tangle at the back post, appeals for an Arsenal penalty, but Gabriel was the first player to pull a shirt.

    Gvardiol with a diagonal cross that floats behind for an Arsenal goal kick. City starting to enjoy some control in the Arsenal half, with Arteta’s team trusting their defensive shape to absorb pressure.

    Arsenal with the chance to counter-attack with runners after Kovacic’s loss of possession in midfield, but Odegaard’s pass was slightly behind Madueke, who then had to check before hesitating. Surely more goals to follow, given the ease with which Arsenal are getting at City and the forward quality in Maresca’s team.

    It has been revealed that odegaard tries a chipped pass into Havertz’s path in the penalty area but Gvardiol heads away. Moments earlier, Doku claimed he was fouled by White near the touchline but nothing doing.

    Arsenal continue to flow forward, finding plenty of space in City’s half, but Tzolis’s cross deflects into the arms of Donnarumma.

    Sources indicate that there was a check for offside in the build up to Arsenal’s goal but the goal stands. Welcome back VAR, and consider the curtain raised on the fresh season. City enjoying some possession since conceding.

    Industry observers note that that’s certainly one way to start a fresh season. It’s a fabulous team goal, with Lewis-Skelly at the heart of it. There has been a lot of talk about this teenager’s future but, in this reporter’s humble opinion, it should not even be a discussion. Losing a player of this quality, a product of the club’s academy, would be a terrible mistake.

    Surely the fastest goal in the history of this fixture, or most fixtures for that matter.

    Arsenal were camped in City’s half from kick off, and it was superb from Lewis-Skelly in midfield to let the ball run across his body and find the run of Calafiori with a reverse pass, and the left-back keeps his cool to roll the ball beyond Donnarumma.

    Riccardo Calafiori gives Arsenal the lead after just 24 seconds 🤯The assist from Myles Lewis-Skelly 👏📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/aU0UsCB1Xs.

    Arsenal get the game, and the 2026-27 domestic season, started.

    Former Man City player Mike Summerbee, who fans used to hail with a Small Faces-inspired chant, is involved in the preliminaries.

    Industry observers note that with no Timber, Saliba or Rice, this could be a more open game than some of the recent chess matches between these sides. The lower stakes should help with that. City have a favourable match up down their left with O’Reilly and Doku against Madueke and White. There is more ball retention in Arsenal’s team than at periods of last season, with Guimaraes, Odegaard, Lewis-Skelly and Havertz in the middle.

    In a recent development, sincere commiserations to the Arsenal and Manchester City supporters who have attempted to travel by road to Cardiff today. We should have nothing but sympathy for those diehards who have tried to navigate the car parks of the M5 and the M4 and nothing but scorn for whoever is in charge of planning at Wembley. Who would have thought to check the football calendar before booking a concert for the week before the new season? A total nonsense. Let’s hope the game turns out to be better than the travel.

    Always a talking point during the Six Nations, but there is no reason for it to close on a sunny afternoon on the banks of the River Taff. That will mean a slightly annoying shadow across the pitch, always a potential irritant in these August or May showpieces.

    I noted already in the last days, no matter if we are in August or May, it is a final and when it is a final we need to win.

    It has been revealed that [Players coming back from the World Cup] Many, many players, for us for them, we are in the exact same situation. It depends how we can manage the game, we will see.

    [What he expects from Anderson] Exactly the player he is. We are not asking him something more. He is a good player on and off the ball, always making an effort for his team-mates.

    Sources indicate that I said in the press conference, we are going to decide the four captains when the window closes. At the moments, Ruben Dias and Erling are with us [no comment on Rodri’s future].

    Good afternoon from Cardiff, where the sun is shining and the fans are enjoying the pubs outside the Principality Stadium. The teams are allowed nine substitutes today, which has really highlighted the bloated nature of Arsenal’s squad. There’s no space for Ethan Nwaneri, Gabriel Martinelli, Gabriel Jesus, Fabio Vieira or Reiss Nelson. All five of them could be sold by the end of the month.

    I had plenty of rest, some work as well, it was a break that I really enjoyed.

    In a recent development, very much [on if he was impressed with his signings]. Christos [Tzolis] came early which always helps with a latest signing, and Bruno joined us last week after a long summer with him but he is in good condition.

    I think it is something very individual. [Declan] Rice played more than 65 games, he needed a complete rest and we need to build him. It’s not only physical, it’s mental freshness. For the players not involved in the World Cup it is a bit different. They remain so competitive. They wanted to be involved and that’s good to see as well.

    According to recent reports, [On Bruno] He is a ball of energy. He has an unbelievable desire to win every ball. You sense he will drive the dressing room and when you bring someone with that competitive nature, it will only drive the boys.

    [On retaining the title] Still recognise the major margins that we have to improve as a team, individually and as well the ambition of the club which is unquestionable.

    It has been revealed that elliot Anderson makes his first City appearance, and he will be partnered by Mateo Kovacic in midfield with Nico O’Reilly drifting into those areas from midfield. Phil Foden, who did not go to the World Cup, starts ahead of Rayan Cherki and Doku, Haaland and Semenyo is City’s strongest front three. No Rodri, but Jack Grealish is on the bench.

    Man City starting XI: Donnarumma; Khusanov, Dias, Gvardiol, O’Reilly; Kovacic, Anderson; Semenyo, Foden, Doku; Haaland.

    Subs: Rulli, Guéhi, Marmoush, Cherki, Nico, Grealish, Aït-Nouri, Nunes, Lewis.

    In a recent development, the other interesting snippets are Arteta plumping for Madueke over Max Dowman on the right, Havertz over Gyokeres and Calafiori over Hincapie. Also worth noting that there is no place in the squad for Ethan Nwaneri nor Gabriel Martinelli who have been linked with moves. The same goes for Fabio Vieira, Gabriel Jesus and Reiss Nelson.

    Arsenal starting XI: Raya; White, Mosquera, Gabriel, Calafiori; Guimaraes, Lewis-Skelly, Odegaard; Madueke, Havertz, Tzolis.

    Subs: Kepa, Hincapie, Rice, Zubimendi, Merino, Eze, Dowman, Saka, Gyokeres.

    🔴 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 ⚪️Mikel names a strong starting XI 👊🤝Presented by @deel pic.twitter.com/bckDyMazRo.

    Sources indicate that declan Rice and Bukayo Saka are with the group, but they have not kicked a ball in pre-season. They are looking at half hour of football at the absolute maximum today.

    According to recent reports, in case any Arsenal fan had forgotten that last season ended with them losing a Champions League final on penalties, City fans are on hand to remind them. They have one European Cup to Arsenal’s zero. Away from the tin foil trophies, I’m sure much bottle-related mirth is on the cards, especially now broadcasters and fans are aware of the viral possibilities. Too aware, I would argue.

    The pool of players who can improve the Premier League champions and Champions League finalists is a small one, but it is still fair to point out that Arsenal’s summer has not gone smoothly. They pursued Morgan Rogers and Vinicius Junior without success, and Arteta’s desire to take the team to a “different dimension” has so far gone unfulfilled., certainly in the forward positions.

    Arsenal still look strong, but have they passed up a chance to pull away from the rest? Sam Wallace takes a look at their summer so far.

    It would have been less stressful for Guardiola to go once he realised the great side of Kevin De Bruyne was nearing its end. Instead he opted to oversee a rebuild that gives his successor a greater chance of immediate success, going close to the title last season in what was effectively year one for a re-emerging City side. Guardiola must have known he was signing Gianluigi Donnarumma, Antoine Semenyo, Marc Guéhi and Rayan Cherki for someone else’s long-term benefit.

    The Community Shield returns to Cardiff’s Principality Stadium for the first time since 2006, and a different dynamic is at play between Arsenal and Manchester City.

    When the two clubs played at Wembley in this fixture three years ago, it felt like a more significant occasion for Arsenal as they sought to prove that the gap was closing to Pep Guardiola’s champions.

    Now it is Arsenal and Mikel Arteta who have a league title behind them, while Enzo Maresca is the manager hoping to build credibility as City turn the page post-Pep Guardiola.

    In truth, these two teams will look very different by the time the season gathers pace in autumn. World Cup exertions mean Elliot Anderson, Erling Haaland, Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka will be minimally involved in this game, while transfer prepares remain up in the air for both camps.

    In a recent development, city appear bound to lose Rodri, in addition to Bernardo Silva and Tijjani Reijnders in central midfield. Rodri’s sale would expedite a move for Lille’s Ayyoub Bouaddi, and possibly Enzo Fernandez despite Chelsea’s insistence that the deadline to sign him for £120m has passed.

    Arsenal are also open for business, hoping to add a right-sided defender to help them cope with William Saliba’s absence. The £75m purchase of Bruno Guimarães means the champions’ midfield options look formidable, but so far it has been another summer without a level-raising forward signing. Christos Tzolis in and Leandro Trossard out looks canny business, but falls into the category of like for like.

    Sources indicate that although Arsenal held their nerve to see off City in the title race, they failed to win in three attempts against their rivals, including a limp defeat in the Carabao Cup final at Wembley. Arsenal also failed to win, or score, against Liverpool in the Premier League last season so their record in the substantial games is an area for improvement.

    The victors this afternoon will claim to have laid a marker down, the losers will write the game off as a warm up exercise.

    #3658. Pelé at the 1970 World Cup: the memories beyond the goals

    📅 02 Jan 2023 • ⏱️ 12m • 📚 Deep Dive (2344 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Thesefootballtimes ↗ Open Full Page

    Pelé at the 1970 World Cup: the memories beyond the goals

    📅 02 Jan 2023 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2344 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thesefootballtimes

    ⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, every four years, strikers from a host of countries converge on that ultimate festival of football: the World Cup.
    • According to recent reports, go right back to 1962 and we see Garrincha score a thundering shot against England in the quarter-finals.
    • Sources indicate that in 1974, Gerd Muller highlights his predatory instincts to spin on a dime and cause Dutch heartache.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, every four years, strikers from a host of countries converge on that ultimate festival of football: the World Cup. For many, this represents the pinnacle of their careers to date, the chance to prove themselves against the best and to write themselves into history. And each World Cup throws up a forward who is forever associated with that competition; often one goal in particular that lives on in collective memories.

    According to recent reports, go right back to 1962 and we see Garrincha score a thundering shot against England in the quarter-finals. 1966 sees an exhausted Geoff Hurst hurtle towards goal before unleashing a piledriver past Hans Tilkowski – a shot that he later admitted was hit as hard as it was so that if he likely missed, it would eat up time recovering the ball.

    Sources indicate that in 1974, Gerd Muller highlights his predatory instincts to spin on a dime and cause Dutch heartache. Four years later, Mario Kempes bursts through the Netherlands defence, hair billowing behind him. The list goes on: Paolo Rossi in 1982 against Brazil; Diego Maradona in 1986 against England; Roberto Baggio in 1990 against Czechoslovakia.

    It has been revealed that what these all have in common is forwards scoring goals that are forever remembered from those respective tournaments and often the first thing that you will think off when someone mentions their name and the competition. If I simply say the words 1998 and Zinedine Zidane, it’s likely your first thought is of his two goals in the final.

    The list above has deliberately excluded one World Cup, the 1970 edition in Mexico. Yes that beautiful World Cup that was the first in colour with the shimmering heat haze and crackling commentary. And if you play the word association game once again and ask someone what first pops into their head when you mention that competition, the likely answer is Brazil.

    Indeed, if you then ask them to name one player from that team, it is odds on they are going to say Pelé. Because while the Brazil side that won the tournament were arguably the greatest national team of all time (Hungary 1954 and the Netherlands 1974 might like to debate that), one player still managed to stand out from such illustrious company.

    In a recent development, just how great a striker was Pelé? Well, let’s start with 501 goals in 493 appearances for Santos between 1956 and 1974 – so yes, averaging a goal a game for 18 years. Ah, but I hear you say, ‘that is in the Brazilian league, which surely is not the same standard as European leagues?’ That is open to debate, particularly given the number of world-class footballers within the competition at the time.

    Let’s then consider Pelé’s international record of 77 goals in 92 games. That includes playing in four World Cups against the top teams of those times. Faced with statistics such as those, it is hard not to argue that Pelé was extremely good at putting the ball into the net.

    Industry observers note that but that leads to an interesting observation. There is no doubt that the 1970 World Cup and Pelé are intertwined in people’s memories. One of the greatest goalscorers of all-time helped his side lift the trophy with four goals across the tournament, but oddly enough if you again ask people the first five things that come into their head when you say Pelé and 1970, I think you would be surprised to find that not a single one of them would be a goal scored by him.

    It has been revealed that unlike the other strikers mentioned earlier, Pelé’s fame in 1970 actually came more from misses than goals. Yes, one of the greatest goalscorers is actually remembered better for misses and saves.

    Brazil’s opening match of the tournament sees them pitted against a decent Czechoslovakia team. The game is only three minutes old when a ball across the area finds Pelé unmarked in front of an open goal, who then proceeds to place the ball over the bar. That miss is then compounded by the Czechs having the cheek to take the lead after just 11 minutes. Things are not going according to blueprint. But Brazil begin to regain their composure and, after 23 minutes, Rivellino thunders in a trademark free-kick.

    In a recent development, as half-time approaches, Pelé receives the ball within the Brazil half and surveys the scene while moving slowly towards the centre circle. Then, suddenly, he smashes the ball goalwards. As the camera follows the flight of the ball, it picks up the Czech goalkeeper, Ivo Viktor, furiously backpedalling. In that split second after receiving the ball, Pelé has noticed Viktor has strayed forward from his goalline and decided to attempt to lob him. The Brazilian commentator describes the action perfectly: “Pele, Pele, Pele … almost,” as the ball just goes wide of the post.

    It is important to bear in mind the context of this attempt. This is not a league match against Wimbledon where you are 2-0 up in injury time, so why the hell not have a go; this is an opening World Cup tie in which you are level. To even attempt such a lob on such a stage shows the audacity of Pelé. That is strengthened by the fact that, even though he actually missed, it is still remembered by all. Yes, David Beckham’s lob was fantastic, but he was standing on the shoulders of Pele.

    Industry observers note that brazil end up with an emphatic 4-1 victory over Czechoslovakia, including a goal from Pelé before being overshadowed by a double from Jairzinho. But they face stiff competition in their group by being drawn alongside the reigning champions England, who arguably have a better team now than in ’66. And so the second match of the group between the two teams is always going to be critical in terms of who advances top.

    It has been revealed that the game kicks off at noon under a scorching Mexican sun – advantage Brazil in terms of weather. Just seeing a red-headed, freckled Alan Ball chasing the ball is the ultimate advert for sun cream.

    Recent findings suggest that just nine minutes into the game, Carlos Alberto moves towards the halfway line with the ball before hitting a great pass into the stride of Jairzinho, who then beats Terry Cooper to take the ball to the byline before hitting a cross to the back post. And there is Pelé, who powers a header downwards towards the corner at a horrible height for any goalkeeper. But the ‘keeper happens to be Gordon Banks, who somehow gets across from the near post to the far. He doesn’t just palm it out but scoops it over the bar. Enter immortality.

    As time progresses, the cult of the Banks save grows. It steadily becomes referred to as the greatest save of all time – as if that is something that anyone is really fit to judge. I personally would argue that Jim Montgomery’s double save against Leeds in the 1973 FA Cup final could give it a run for its money. But the moniker has stuck – aided in England by David Coleman’s commentary of the save being sampled into ‘Three Lions’.

    Industry observers note that they say a picture tells a thousand words. During the course of football history, there have been many iconic images – Maradona facing five Belgian defenders or Baggio hands on hips after his penalty miss – but one of the most famous is that of Pelé and Bobby Moore embracing at the end of the Brazil-England game. Embracing may be too strong a word given that it involves an Englishman in the 1970s, but there is a definite tenderness in the way Pelé touches Moore’s face while the latter clutches the Brazilian’s discarded shirt proudly in his hand.

    According to recent reports, it is an image of two legendary players who know that they have just been involved in a titanic struggle. It is an image of pure mutual respect. After all, in a game that, according to the English, had already produced “the greatest save of all time”, it had also, according to the English once again, produced “the greatest tackle of all time” by Moore on Jairzinho. It’s another moment sampled into ‘Three Lions’, ensuring it lives on for generations.

    Sources indicate that brazil end up winning all their group games and then proceed to eliminate a useful Peru side in the quarter-finals. Standing between them and a World Cup final are their old foes, Uruguay. It has to be remembered that it was Uruguay who crushed the Brazilian nation by defeating them 2-1 in the 1950 World Cup at the Maracanã. Therefore any significant game against Uruguay was always going to cause heightened tension for fans of O Seleção.

    Recent findings suggest that the game did not disappoint in that respect with Uruguay taking an early lead. As the half wore on, thoughts must have been flooding back to 1950. Surely Brazil’s greatest side weren’t going to be undone by their tiny neighbours again? But an equaliser just before half-time helped soothe frayed nerves.

    Sources indicate that with 15 minutes remaining, Brazil finally take the lead through a beautiful Jairzinho goal. A sigh of relief ripples through their fans, but is tempered by the memory that they also led at one stage during the Maracanazo. And so nerves continue to jangle until, with just one minute remaining, Pelé runs at the Uruguayan defence before setting up Rivellino to put the game beyond doubt.

    As injury time commences, Brazil look home and dry. As the crowd awaits the final whistle, a through ball from Tostão puts Pelé though onto goal. The goalkeeper, Ladislao Mazurkiewicz, rushes out but it appears that Pelé will get to the ball first. Then it should just be a matter of touching it past the ‘keeper and rolling the ball into the unguarded net for the icing on the cake.

    But this is Pelé, a player whose genius almost produced a halfway-line goal earlier in the tournament. To just go around the ‘keeper would be too straightforward. After all, Brazil have won the game. So instead, while running at full speed, Pelé just steps over the ball and lets it run on past a stunned Mazurkiewicz who is stranded in no-man’s land. Quick as you like, Pelé then spins to the right to chase the ball, hits it towards the net, and watches the ball roll agonisingly just wide of the post. It is a move that takes the breath away in a similar fashion to the Cruyff turn in 1974 and is perhaps the greatest goal that never was.

    And so Brazil progress to the World Cup final and a date with Italy. The biggest stage in world football. After 18 minutes, Pelé opens the scoring with a header at the far post. But an equaliser by Roberto Boninsegna – he of the Coke can fame – sees the sides level at half-time. Thereafter, goals from Gerson and Jairzinho put Brazil firmly back in the driving seat.As the match approaches the end, Brazilian songs fill the Mexican air.

    But there is one more moment of greatness to savour. Brazil retrieve the ball near their own penalty area and start to pass it around with one-touch football. The ball falls to Clodoaldo who almost drunkenly weaves past four Italian players before laying it off to Rivellino, who immediately passes it directly forward to the feet of Jairzinho. He brings the ball across the penalty area and then spots Pelé to his right. A short pass later and O Rei has the ball facing the goal just outside the area with an Italian defender before him.

    We’ve all tried it during five-a-side or a Sunday league game – the infamous no-look pass. It is up there with the nutmeg as the ultimate flashy move. With a sixth sense, Pelé just holds the ball momentarily while, behind him, Carlos Alberto is streaking forward on his right-hand side. A heartbeat later and Pelé rolls the ball so, so casually to the right, sensing that Alberto is arriving. And without having to break stride at all, he drills the ball in at full speed. Brazil are world champions once again.

    And the final, iconic images of the World Cup are of Brazilian fans rushing onto the field and basically stripping the players of all their kit as souvenirs. Pelé is down to his shorts before being hoisted aloft by fans and paraded around the stadium.

    The Brazil team of 1970 was undoubtedly one of the greatest of all, setting a benchmark that has haunted subsequent Seleção sides for generations. And while the whole squad was fantastic, Pelé will always be remembered as the focal point. His four goals, including one in the final, helped push Brazil to victory, just like his goals had 12 years earlier in Sweden. And they were great goals, especially his first against Czechoslovakia.

    It has been revealed that but Pelé was such an outstanding player that it is more than just his goals that are remembered from 1970. Only Pelé would have the audacity to try to lob the goalkeeper from his own half. Only Pelé would have the nerve to dummy an onrushing ‘keeper and then retrieve the ball and almost score. Only Pelé could power a header so hard and so perfectly into the bottom corner that the resulting save would be described as the greatest save of all time. And only Pelé could finish off the greatest World Cup final team goal with a no-look pass to a colleague.

    Pelé was an outstanding goalscorer but also, unlike many other greats in front of goal, so much more. It really wasn’t just about what he did that made him great; it is also the time and place that he did it. That’s what gets results.

    Latest Update: Liverpool must make January signing after telling Trey Nyoni comments

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (548 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Empireofthekop

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Trey Nyoni has admitted he ‘enjoys’ playing in the six position, but that it’s still a ‘new position’ for him.
    • The young Englishman has caught the eye with his performances at L4 this term, earning three straight starts across clashes with Arsenal (Premier League), Chelsea (Carabao Cup) and Fenerbahce (Champions League).
    • However, the teenager’s admission ultimately raises concerns around the midfield department ahead of the January transfer window.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Trey Nyoni has admitted he ‘enjoys’ playing in the six position, but that it’s still a ‘new position’ for him.

    The young Englishman has caught the eye with his performances at L4 this term, earning three straight starts across clashes with Arsenal (Premier League), Chelsea (Carabao Cup) and Fenerbahce (Champions League).

    However, the teenager’s admission ultimately raises concerns around the midfield department ahead of the January transfer window.

    It’s reassuring that links to Lamine Camara (who came close to a switch to Chelsea in the summer) have resurfaced ahead of the winter, given ongoing concerns over how Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch fit in an Andoni Iraola side.

    While the performances of Alexis Mac Allister and Nyoni have undoubtedly mitigated matters, the truth of the matter is that Liverpool can’t look to rely on the latter of the duo throughout an entire campaign.

    The Reds must, and no doubt will, look after the teenager to ensure his excellent development carries on smoothly, but his recent comments are a clear reminder that investment midway through the campaign is a necessity.

    “I’ve been playing like a number six. I played there when I was young but, to be honest, it’s a fresh position for me. I’ve had to learn a lot in a short space of time,” Nyoni told The Inside Scoop (via BBC Sport).

    “I enjoy playing like a six because I can get on the ball and always try to play forwards, but I enjoy playing as an eight as well.

    “I like to drop in, get the ball and play forward but I’ve had to learn the discipline of being a number six.

    It has been revealed that “Right now, I don’t really have a preference. As I’m starting out, I enjoy playing both.”.

    Industry observers note that we have faith that Iraola’s demands will eventually click with Gravenberch and Szoboszlai, but it’s still painful to see how open Liverpool look in the middle of the park when Mac Allister is forced to share space with either of his senior midfield partners. And the less said about a double pivot consisting of the Dutchman and the Hungarian, the better.

    Yes, it’s fair to point out that our season is far from spiralling under Iraola — the Reds sit fourth in the Premier League table with only four points standing between them and Fabian Hurzeler’s high-flying Brighton in second.

    Industry observers note that but it does feel like there is an opportunity for Liverpool to make a modest statement in 2026/27. Not quite title glory, it has to be said, but certainly to stake a claim as “best of the rest” and set a promising foundation for the seasons to come under Iraola.

    Adding an additional midfielder (like, cough cough, Lamine Camara, cough cough) to the ranks who can carry out the Basque’s demands would undoubtedly serve that purpose.

    Elsewhere, the backline looks in fine shape and the forward line evidently needs time to gel. Give the manager the tools he needs in midfield and this could be an impressive opening campaign for Andoni Iraola.
